### 2. Clearing Custom Data via Crafting

Standard shaped and shapeless recipes in Minecraft automatically copy components from matching item stacks if not explicitly cleared. To make a recipe that specifically strips the custom configuration data (wiping the blueprint), you can create a custom `CraftingRecipe` class.

Create a new class named **`BlueprintWipeRecipe.java`**:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.recipe;

import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.ModItems;
import net.minecraft.core.HolderLookup;
import net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.CraftingBookCategory;
import net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.CraftingInput;
import net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.CustomRecipe;
import net.minecraft.world.level.Level;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

public class BlueprintWipeRecipe extends CustomRecipe {
    public BlueprintWipeRecipe(CraftingBookCategory category) {
        super(category);
    }

    @Override
    public boolean matches(@NotNull CraftingInput input, @NotNull Level level) {
        int blueprintCount = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < input.size(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = input.getItem(i);
            if (!stack.isEmpty()) {
                if (stack.is(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get())) {
                    blueprintCount++;
                } else {
                    return false; // Only allow the blueprint in the grid
                }
            }
        }
        return blueprintCount == 1;
    }

    @Override
    public @NotNull ItemStack assemble(@NotNull CraftingInput input, HolderLookup.@NotNull Provider registries) {
        for (int i = 0; i < input.size(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = input.getItem(i);
            if (stack.is(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get())) {
                // Return a fresh, empty blueprint stack without custom data
                ItemStack cleanBlueprint = new ItemStack(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get());
                cleanBlueprint.remove(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
                return cleanBlueprint;
            }
        }
        return ItemStack.EMPTY;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean canCraftInDimensions(int width, int height) {
        return width * height >= 1;
    }

    @Override
    public net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.RecipeSerializer<?> getSerializer() {
        // Register this serializer in your RecipeSerializers registry
        return null; 
    }
}
```

*Verification:* Once your serializer is registered and wired up, placing any configured blueprint back into the crafting grid will strip its stored configuration data and return a pristine, reusable blank blueprint.

### Gemini

That Factorio-style workflow is a clean and intuitive design for modded Minecraft logistics.

### 1. Data Serialization Structure

Storing the blueprint data inside the `CUSTOM_DATA` component of the `BlueprintItem` stack makes the data compact and easily transferable.

Because the `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity` inventory handler only allows valid modules in its 27 slots, you do not need complex pre-filtering logic when copying. The blueprint can serialize the grid into a compound tag structure like this:

```
BlueprintData: {
  SlotCount: 27,
  Slots: [
    { Slot: 0, Item: "praeteritum_futurum:inventory_module", CustomData: {...} },
    { Slot: 1, Item: "praeteritum_futurum:io_module", CustomData: { FaceModes: {...} } },
    ...
  ]
}
```

### 2. Item Tooltip Summary

To keep the hover tooltip clean and avoid clogging the screen with 27 individual slot descriptions, reading the serialized NBT on hover and displaying a aggregated bill of materials works best:

```
Blueprint: Automated Smelter Array
Requires:
  - 1x Inventory Module
  - 2x IO Module
  - 1x Smelting Module
  - 1x Filter Module
```

### 3. Copy/Paste Logic Rules & Constraints

#### **Copying (Right-click Machine Framework):**

- Scans the 27 module slots of the targeted `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity`.
- Serializes every module's item ID and its exact `CUSTOM_DATA` (face modes, filter lists, config slots) into the blueprint stack.
- Triggers a status message in the action bar: `"Blueprint copied!"` along with a quick click sound.

#### **Pasting (Right-click Machine Framework with Written Blueprint):**

- **Empty Machine Check:** Restricting pasting to completely empty machine frameworks prevents accidental overwrites or module loss. If the machine already contains modules, send a message: `"Machine framework must be empty to apply blueprint."`
- **Module & Data Validation:**
  - The system counts the required modules from the blueprint.
  - It checks the player's inventory for matching module stacks.
  - **Blank Module Enforcement:** To prevent destroying existing module configurations, the paste operation checks that the candidate modules in the player's inventory do **not** carry existing `CUSTOM_DATA`. If a player only has pre-configured modules, display a message: `"Missing blank modules in inventory: Requires 2x IO Module (Clean)."`
- **Execution:**
  - Consumes the required blank modules from the player's inventory.
  - Installs each module into its designated slot in the `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity` and writes the saved `CUSTOM_DATA` onto the block entity / module stack.
  - Displays an action bar message: `"Blueprint applied!"`

### Gemini

To guarantee that player interaction and blueprint usage cause **zero server lag spikes, minimal memory allocations, and zero network bloat**, we can design the logic around optimized NBT and NeoForge Data Component practices.

## ⚡ Performance & Optimization Strategies

### 1. Minimal NBT Serialization (Memory & Garbage Collection)

- **Skip Empty Slots:** Never store empty slots in NBT. Out of 27 machine slots, if a player only uses 4, the blueprint NBT array will only contain 4 tags instead of 27.
- **Direct Component Copying:** In Minecraft 1.21.1, rather than re-parsing item stacks or converting deep tags back and forth, we extract and copy only the necessary `CUSTOM_DATA` component directly from the installed module stack.

### 2. Fast Player Inventory Scanning (Single-Pass Lookup)

- **Single-Pass Inventory Counting:** When checking if a player has the required modules, scan the player inventory array **once** to build a lightweight summary count instead of repeatedly searching through 36 player slots for each blueprint slot.
- **Primitive Array Data:** Use raw primitive data arrays (e.g., `CompoundTag` lists with integer slot mappings) to avoid object instantiation overhead during pasting.

### 3. Server-Side Execution Guard (Ping & Network Safety)

- **Server-Only Processing:** Execute all copying and pasting calculations exclusively on the server thread (`!level.isClientSide()`). The client only sends the standard right-click packet, resulting in **zero network payload overhead** or custom packet spam.
- **Action Bar Feedback:** Use client action bar messages (`player.displayClientMessage(..., true)`) so notification text doesn't bloat the chat log or client memory.

## 📜 Complete `BlueprintItem.java` Implementation

Here is the fully optimized implementation for `BlueprintItem.java`:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom;

import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.core.HolderLookup;
import net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents;
import net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag;
import net.minecraft.nbt.ListTag;
import net.minecraft.nbt.Tag;
import net.minecraft.network.chat.Component;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer;
import net.minecraft.sounds.SoundEvents;
import net.minecraft.sounds.SoundSource;
import net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult;
import net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player;
import net.minecraft.world.item.Item;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.item.TooltipFlag;
import net.minecraft.world.item.context.UseOnContext;
import net.minecraft.world.item.component.CustomData;
import net.minecraft.world.level.Level;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity;
import net.neoforged.neoforge.registries.BuiltInRegistries;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.*;

public class BlueprintItem extends Item {

    public BlueprintItem(Properties properties) {
        super(properties);
    }

    @Override
    public @NotNull InteractionResult useOn(UseOnContext context) {
        Level level = context.getLevel();
        BlockPos pos = context.getClickedPos();
        Player player = context.getPlayer();
        ItemStack blueprintStack = context.getItemInHand();

        if (player == null) return InteractionResult.PASS;

        BlockEntity be = level.getBlockEntity(pos);
        if (!(be instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine)) {
            return InteractionResult.PASS;
        }

        // Server-side execution only to keep network payload minimal
        if (!level.isClientSide()) {
            HolderLookup.Provider registries = level.registryAccess();
            boolean isSneaking = player.isShiftKeyDown();

            // Shift + Right Click = Copy Machine Layout to Blueprint
            if (isSneaking) {
                copyMachineToBlueprint(machine, blueprintStack, player, registries);
            } 
            // Right Click = Paste Blueprint Configuration to Machine
            else {
                pasteBlueprintToMachine(machine, blueprintStack, player, registries);
            }
        }

        return InteractionResult.sidedSuccess(level.isClientSide());
    }

    /**
     * Serializes the machine's module layout into the blueprint stack's CUSTOM_DATA.
     */
    private void copyMachineToBlueprint(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine, ItemStack blueprint, Player player, HolderLookup.Provider registries) {
        ListTag slotList = new ListTag();
        int moduleCount = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < 27; i++) {
            ItemStack module = machine.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i);
            if (!module.isEmpty()) {
                moduleCount++;
                CompoundTag slotTag = new CompoundTag();
                slotTag.putInt("Slot", i);
                slotTag.putString("Item", BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.getKey(module.getItem()).toString());

                // Copy custom data (config/filters/modes) if present
                CustomData customData = module.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
                if (customData != null) {
                    slotTag.put("CustomData", customData.copyTag());
                }

                slotList.add(slotTag);
            }
        }

        if (moduleCount == 0) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cCannot copy: Targeted machine framework is empty!"), true);
            return;
        }

        // Store serialized data in Blueprint's CUSTOM_DATA component
        CustomData.update(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, blueprint, tag -> {
            tag.put("BlueprintLayout", slotList);
        });

        player.level().playSound(null, player.getX(), player.getY(), player.getZ(), SoundEvents.UI_CARTOGRAPHY_TABLE_TAKE_RESULT, SoundSource.PLAYERS, 0.8F, 1.2F);
        player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§aBlueprint copied! Recorded " + moduleCount + " modules."), true);
    }

    /**
     * Applies saved layout onto an empty machine, consuming matching blank modules from player inventory.
     */
    private void pasteBlueprintToMachine(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine, ItemStack blueprint, Player player, HolderLookup.Provider registries) {
        CustomData customData = blueprint.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
        if (customData == null || !customData.copyTag().contains("BlueprintLayout")) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cBlueprint is blank! Shift + Right-Click a configured machine first."), true);
            return;
        }

        // Rule 1: Target machine must be completely empty of modules
        boolean hasModulesInstalled = false;
        for (int i = 0; i < 27; i++) {
            if (!machine.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i).isEmpty()) {
                hasModulesInstalled = true;
                break;
            }
        }

        if (hasModulesInstalled) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cTarget Machine Framework must be empty to apply a blueprint!"), true);
            return;
        }

        ListTag slotList = customData.copyTag().getList("BlueprintLayout", Tag.TAG_COMPOUND);
        if (slotList.isEmpty()) return;

        // Rule 2: Single-pass inventory scan for clean/unconfigured modules
        Map<Item, Integer> requiredModules = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
            CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
            ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
            Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);
            requiredModules.put(item, requiredModules.getOrDefault(item, 0) + 1);
        }

        Map<Item, Integer> availableCleanModules = countCleanModulesInInventory(player);

        // Check if player has all required clean modules
        for (Map.Entry<Item, Integer> entry : requiredModules.entrySet()) {
            Item requiredItem = entry.getKey();
            int neededCount = entry.getValue();
            int availableCount = availableCleanModules.getOrDefault(requiredItem, 0);

            if (availableCount < neededCount) {
                String itemName = new ItemStack(requiredItem).getHoverName().getString();
                player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cMissing modules: Needs " + neededCount + "x " + itemName + " (Clean)."), true);
                return;
            }
        }

        // Rule 3: Consume items from inventory & install into block entity
        for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
            CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
            int slotIndex = slotTag.getInt("Slot");
            ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
            Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);

            // Deduct 1 clean module stack from player inventory
            consumeCleanModule(player, item);

            // Construct installed stack with stored data components
            ItemStack newModuleStack = new ItemStack(item);
            if (slotTag.contains("CustomData")) {
                newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, CustomData.of(slotTag.getCompound("CustomData")));
                newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.MAX_STACK_SIZE, 1);
            }

            // Install into machine framework entity
            machine.getModuleHandler().setStackInSlot(slotIndex, newModuleStack);
        }

        machine.setChanged();
        player.level().playSound(null, machine.getBlockPos(), SoundEvents.ITEM_FRAME_ADD_ITEM, SoundSource.BLOCKS, 0.8F, 1.1F);
        player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§aBlueprint applied successfully!"), true);
    }

    /**
     * Counts unconfigured (clean) module stacks in the player's inventory.
     */
    private Map<Item, Integer> countCleanModulesInInventory(Player player) {
        Map<Item, Integer> cleanCounts = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < player.getInventory().getContainerSize(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = player.getInventory().getItem(i);
            if (!stack.isEmpty() && isCleanModule(stack)) {
                cleanCounts.put(stack.getItem(), cleanCounts.getOrDefault(stack.getItem(), 0) + stack.getCount());
            }
        }
        return cleanCounts;
    }

    /**
     * Consumes a single clean module stack from the player's inventory.
     */
    private void consumeCleanModule(Player player, Item targetItem) {
        for (int i = 0; i < player.getInventory().getContainerSize(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = player.getInventory().getItem(i);
            if (!stack.isEmpty() && stack.is(targetItem) && isCleanModule(stack)) {
                stack.shrink(1);
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Verifies if a module item carries no custom configuration tags.
     */
    private boolean isCleanModule(ItemStack stack) {
        CustomData customData = stack.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
        return customData == null || customData.copyTag().isEmpty();
    }

    @Override
    public void appendHoverText(@NotNull ItemStack stack, Item.@NotNull TooltipContext context, @NotNull List<Component> tooltipComponents, @NotNull TooltipFlag tooltipFlag) {
        CustomData customData = stack.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
        if (customData != null && customData.copyTag().contains("BlueprintLayout")) {
            ListTag slotList = customData.copyTag().getList("BlueprintLayout", Tag.TAG_COMPOUND);

            Map<Item, Integer> summary = new HashMap<>();
            for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
                CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
                ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
                Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);
                summary.put(item, summary.getOrDefault(item, 0) + 1);
            }

            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§7Stored Configuration:"));
            for (Map.Entry<Item, Integer> entry : summary.entrySet()) {
                String itemName = new ItemStack(entry.getKey()).getHoverName().getString();
                tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8 • §f" + entry.getValue() + "x §e" + itemName));
            }
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8Clear in crafting table to wipe data."));
        } else {
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§7Status: §cEmpty"));
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8Shift + Right-Click a machine to copy."));
        }

        super.appendHoverText(stack, context, tooltipComponents, tooltipFlag);
    }
}
```

### You

hmm how come some of these are like... basic, with existing parent, what's the difference

### Gemini

The difference comes down to shorthand convenience versus explicit model template control.

### 1. `basicItem(...)`

`basicItem` is a built-in helper method that automatically assigns the standard flat `item/generated` parent model and maps the texture using the item registry name. Items like `SALVAGE_SCRAP` use this because they are simple flat items that require no special hand positioning.

### 2. `withExistingParent(...)`

`withExistingParent` gives you direct control over which base model template your item uses.

- **Handheld Tools (`item/handheld`):** Items like `YOOL` and `SALVAGE_CUTTER` use the `item/handheld` parent template. This template rotates and positions the item model correctly in the player hand so it renders like a handheld tool or weapon instead of a flat 2D sprite.
- **Modules (`item/generated`):** The module items use `item/generated` with explicit texture paths to keep their custom layer structure organized.

### Don't Forget Your Blueprint Item Model!

Since you just added the **Blueprint** item, make sure to add it to your `ModItemModelProvider` as well:

```java
basicItem(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get());
```

### Gemini

## 1. Right-Click Opening Machine UI (Block Entity Interaction)

In Minecraft, when a Block Entity implements `MenuProvider` (or handles right-clicks in `use(...)`), right-clicking standard blocks opens their container GUI.

When right-clicking with a blueprint, the machine block intercepts the click before `Item#useOn` can execute. To bypass this, you need to check if the player is holding a `BlueprintItem` inside `MachineFrameworkBlock#useWithoutItem` (or `useItemOn`) and let the item handle the interaction instead:

```java
// Inside MachineFrameworkBlock.java:
@Override
protected InteractionResult useWithoutItem(BlockState state, Level level, BlockPos pos, Player player, BlockHitResult hitResult) {
    ItemStack heldItem = player.getItemInHand(player.getUsedItemHand());
    
    // If holding a Blueprint, let the blueprint item handle the interaction!
    if (heldItem.is(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get())) {
        return InteractionResult.PASS;
    }

    if (!level.isClientSide()) {
        BlockEntity blockEntity = level.getBlockEntity(pos);
        if (blockEntity instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine) {
            player.openMenu(machine);
        }
    }
    return InteractionResult.sidedSuccess(level.isClientSide());
}
```

## 2. Creative Mode Bypass (Infinite Pasting)

In Creative mode (`player.isCreative()`), the inventory check and item consumption logic should be bypassed so you can paste configurations freely without needing items in your hotbar or main inventory.

Update the inventory validation in `BlueprintItem.java`:

```java
// Inside pasteBlueprintToMachine(...) in BlueprintItem.java:

// Creative mode bypass: skip inventory requirement checks
if (!player.isCreative()) {
    Map<Item, Integer> availableCleanModules = countCleanModulesInInventory(player);

    for (Map.Entry<Item, Integer> entry : requiredModules.entrySet()) {
        Item requiredItem = entry.getKey();
        int neededCount = entry.getValue();
        int availableCount = availableCleanModules.getOrDefault(requiredItem, 0);

        if (availableCount < neededCount) {
            String itemName = new ItemStack(requiredItem).getHoverName().getString();
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cMissing modules: Needs " + neededCount + "x " + itemName + " (Clean)."), true);
            return;
        }
    }
}

// Applying modules to machine:
for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
    CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
    int slotIndex = slotTag.getInt("Slot");
    ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
    Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);

    // Only consume modules in Survival mode
    if (!player.isCreative()) {
        consumeCleanModule(player, item);
    }

    ItemStack newModuleStack = new ItemStack(item);
    if (slotTag.contains("CustomData")) {
        newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, CustomData.of(slotTag.getCompound("CustomData")));
        newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.MAX_STACK_SIZE, 1);
    }

    machine.getModuleHandler().setStackInSlot(slotIndex, newModuleStack);
}
```

## 3. Blueprint Wipe Recipe Fix

The crafting table output is empty in your screenshot because standard recipes expect matching outputs or dynamic recipe serializers.

To enable single-item blueprint wiping directly in the grid without setting up a full custom JSON recipe serializer immediately, register a custom `RecipeSerializer` for `BlueprintWipeRecipe` or use a standard Shapeless Recipe with data component clearing.

### Option A: Clean Shapeless Blueprint Reset (Datagen)

In `ModRecipeProvider.java`, register a 1:1 recipe where crafting a blueprint by itself returns a fresh blueprint:

```java
// Wiping blueprint in crafting grid
ShapelessRecipeBuilder.shapeless(RecipeCategory.MISC, ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get())
        .requires(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get())
        .unlockedBy("has_blueprint", has(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get()))
        .save(recipeOutput, ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "blueprint_wipe"));
```

### Option B: Custom Recipe Class

If you prefer using `BlueprintWipeRecipe.java`, register its serializer in a registry class (e.g., `ModRecipes.java`):

```java
public static final DeferredRegister<RecipeSerializer<?>> RECIPE_SERIALIZERS = 
        DeferredRegister.create(Registries.RECIPE_SERIALIZER, PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID);

public static final DeferredHolder<RecipeSerializer<?>, SimpleCraftingRecipeSerializer<BlueprintWipeRecipe>> BLUEPRINT_WIPE =
        RECIPE_SERIALIZERS.register("blueprint_wipe", () -> new SimpleCraftingRecipeSerializer<>(BlueprintWipeRecipe::new));
```

And in `recipeOutput` data gen:

```java
SpecialRecipeBuilder.special(BlueprintWipeRecipe::new)
        .save(recipeOutput, "blueprint_wipe");
```

```java
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

public class MachineFrameworkBlock extends BaseEntityBlock {
    public static final MapCodec<MachineFrameworkBlock> CODEC = simpleCodec(MachineFrameworkBlock::new);

    public MachineFrameworkBlock(Properties properties) {
        super(properties);
    }

    @Override
    @NotNull
    public MapCodec<? extends BaseEntityBlock> codec() {
        return CODEC;
    }

    @Override
    protected @NotNull RenderShape getRenderShape(@NotNull BlockState state) {
        return RenderShape.MODEL;
    }

    @Nullable
    @Override
    public BlockEntity newBlockEntity(@NotNull BlockPos pos, @NotNull BlockState state) {
        return new MachineFrameworkBlockEntity(pos, state);
    }

    @Override
    protected @NotNull ItemInteractionResult useItemOn(@NotNull ItemStack stack, @NotNull BlockState state, Level level, @NotNull BlockPos pos, @NotNull Player player, @NotNull InteractionHand hand, @NotNull BlockHitResult hitResult) {
        // If holding a Blueprint, pass interaction through so BlueprintItem#useOn can handle it
        if (stack.is(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get())) {
            return ItemInteractionResult.PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION;
        }

        if (!level.isClientSide && player instanceof net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer serverPlayer) {
            BlockEntity blockEntity = level.getBlockEntity(pos);
            if (blockEntity instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity frameworkEntity) {
                if (stack.is(ModItems.YOOL.get())) {
                    level.playSound(null, pos, SoundEvents.LEVER_CLICK, net.minecraft.sounds.SoundSource.BLOCKS, 1.0F, 1.0F);
                    serverPlayer.openMenu(frameworkEntity, buf -> buf.writeBlockPos(pos));
                    return ItemInteractionResult.SUCCESS;
                }

                serverPlayer.openMenu(new MenuProvider() {
                    @Override
                    public net.minecraft.network.chat.@NotNull Component getDisplayName() {
                        return frameworkEntity.getDisplayName();
                    }

                    @Override
                    public AbstractContainerMenu createMenu(int containerId, @NotNull Inventory playerInventory, @NotNull Player player) {
                        return frameworkEntity.createInfoMenu(containerId, playerInventory, player);
                    }
                }, buf -> buf.writeBlockPos(pos));
                return ItemInteractionResult.SUCCESS;
            }
        }
        return ItemInteractionResult.PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION;
    }

    @Override
    protected @NotNull InteractionResult useWithoutItem(@NotNull BlockState state, Level level, @NotNull BlockPos pos, @NotNull Player player, @NotNull BlockHitResult hitResult) {
        if (!level.isClientSide && player instanceof net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer serverPlayer) {
            BlockEntity blockEntity = level.getBlockEntity(pos);
            if (blockEntity instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity frameworkEntity) {
                // Empty hand right-click opens the Machine Info Menu (Machine Mode UI)
                serverPlayer.openMenu(new MenuProvider() {
                    @Override
                    public @NotNull Component getDisplayName() {
                        return frameworkEntity.getDisplayName();
                    }

                    @Override
                    public AbstractContainerMenu createMenu(int containerId, @NotNull Inventory playerInventory, @NotNull Player player) {
                        return frameworkEntity.createInfoMenu(containerId, playerInventory, player);
                    }
                }, buf -> buf.writeBlockPos(pos));
                return InteractionResult.SUCCESS;
            }
        }
        return InteractionResult.SUCCESS;
    }

    @Override
    public void onRemove(BlockState state, @NotNull Level level, @NotNull BlockPos pos, BlockState newState, boolean movedByPiston) {
        if (!state.is(newState.getBlock())) {
            BlockEntity blockEntity = level.getBlockEntity(pos);
            if (blockEntity instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity frameworkEntity) {
                net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandler inventoryHandler = frameworkEntity.getInventoryHandler();
                for (int i = 0; i < inventoryHandler.getSlots(); i++) {
                    net.minecraft.world.Containers.dropItemStack(level, pos.getX(), pos.getY(), pos.getZ(), inventoryHandler.getStackInSlot(i));
                }

                net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandler moduleHandler = frameworkEntity.getModuleHandler();
                for (int i = 0; i < moduleHandler.getSlots(); i++) {
                    net.minecraft.world.Containers.dropItemStack(level, pos.getX(), pos.getY(), pos.getZ(), moduleHandler.getStackInSlot(i));
                }

                level.updateNeighbourForOutputSignal(pos, this);
            }
        }
        super.onRemove(state, level, pos, newState, movedByPiston);
    }

    @Nullable
    @Override
    public <T extends BlockEntity> net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntityTicker<T> getTicker(
            @NotNull net.minecraft.world.level.Level level,
            @NotNull BlockState state,
            @NotNull net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntityType<T> blockEntityType
    ) {
        return level.isClientSide() ? null : BaseEntityBlock.createTickerHelper(
                blockEntityType,
                ModBlockEntities.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK_BE.get(),
                MachineFrameworkBlockEntity::serverTick
        );
    }
}
```

### Gemini

Having custom tags like `#praeteritum_futurum:blueprints` is essential for compatibility and maintainability across your codebase.

### Why Keep the Blueprint Tag?

1. **Tag-based Ingredient Matching in Custom Recipes:** Standard Minecraft shapeless recipe builders do not strip Data Components on output automatically. When using custom recipe implementations (such as a custom `SpecialRecipeBuilder`), referencing `Ingredient.of(ModTags.Items.BLUEPRINTS)` in code or datagen allows your recipe logic to match *any* blueprint item registered in that tag.
2. **Cross-Mod Compatibility (Interoperability):** If another mod developer adds an "Advanced Blueprint" or integrates with your machine framework, tagging blueprints allows external mods (or addons) to interact with your blueprint APIs seamlessly without hardcoding specific class checks.
3. **Future Expansion:** If you add tiered blueprints later (e.g., *Gold Blueprint*, *Ender Blueprint*), any tag checks in your block entities or inventory filters will immediately accept them.

### What Good Modding Practices Recommend

In modern NeoForge mod development, standard practice splits handling these scenarios into two main approaches:

#### 1. Reusing a General Custom Recipe Serializer (Recommended for Data-Clearing)

Instead of creating a separate dynamic JSON file for *every* configurable item type (like `module_cleaning.json` or `blueprint_cleaning.json`), clean mod architecture creates **one flexible custom recipe serializer** (e.g., `DataWipeRecipe` or `ComponentResetRecipe`).

This custom recipe checks if the input item matches a specific tag (`#praeteritum_futurum:configurable_modules` or `#praeteritum_futurum:blueprints`), strips the `CUSTOM_DATA` component, and outputs a clean version of the same item.

- **Why it's clean:** You write the serializer logic **once**, and then you can register wiping recipes for modules, blueprints, or future tools with single-line declarations in your `ModRecipeProvider`:

```java
// Example: Using a custom recipe builder backed by tag ingredients
SpecialRecipeBuilder.special(BlueprintWipeRecipe::new)
        .save(recipeOutput, "blueprint_wipe");
```

#### 2. Cauldron or Water-Based Cleaning (Alternative Popular Pattern)

Many tech mods (such as Create or Industrial Foregoing) utilize in-world interactions like **right-clicking a Water Cauldron** with a configured blueprint or module to wash away its data components.

- **Why players like it:** It saves crafting grid space, feels tactile in-game, and avoids needing a dedicated recipe serializer for single-item component resets.

### Summary Recommendation for Your Architecture

Keep your `ModTags.Items.BLUEPRINTS` definition. For recipe cleaning, the most idiomatic pattern is using your custom recipe serializer (`SpecialRecipeBuilder`) inside `ModRecipeProvider`—passing the `ModTags.Items.BLUEPRINTS` ingredient to clear the `CUSTOM_DATA` component when crafted.

### Gemini

To keep your codebase consistent, you can unify the cleaning logic for both configurable modules and blueprints into a single shared custom recipe system. Your existing custom recipe type uses the `praeteritum_futurum:module_cleaning` identifier, which you can expand to handle blueprints alongside modules by utilizing item tags.

### Unified Data Wipe Recipe Class

Instead of writing separate cleaning classes for every item type, a single `DataWipeRecipe` class checks whether an input item belongs to either the configurable modules tag or the blueprints tag. If the item matches, the recipe strips the custom data component and returns a pristine item stack.

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.recipe;

import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.ModTags;
import net.minecraft.core.HolderLookup;
import net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.CraftingBookCategory;
import net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.CraftingInput;
import net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.CustomRecipe;
import net.minecraft.world.item.crafting.RecipeSerializer;
import net.minecraft.world.level.Level;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

public class DataWipeRecipe extends CustomRecipe {
    public DataWipeRecipe(CraftingBookCategory category) {
        super(category);
    }

    @Override
    public boolean matches(@NotNull CraftingInput input, @NotNull Level level) {
        int validItemCount = 0;
        for (int i = 0; i < input.size(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = input.getItem(i);
            if (!stack.isEmpty()) {
                if (stack.is(ModTags.Items.CONFIGURABLE_MODULES) || stack.is(ModTags.Items.BLUEPRINTS)) {
                    validItemCount++;
                } else {
                    return false;
                }
            }
        }
        return validItemCount == 1;
    }

    @Override
    public @NotNull ItemStack assemble(@NotNull CraftingInput input, HolderLookup.@NotNull Provider registries) {
        for (int i = 0; i < input.size(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = input.getItem(i);
            if (stack.is(ModTags.Items.CONFIGURABLE_MODULES) || stack.is(ModTags.Items.BLUEPRINTS)) {
                ItemStack cleanStack = new ItemStack(stack.getItem());
                cleanStack.remove(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
                return cleanStack;
            }
        }
        return ItemStack.EMPTY;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean canCraftInDimensions(int width, int height) {
        return width * height >= 1;
    }

    @Override
    public @NotNull RecipeSerializer<?> getSerializer() {
        return ModRecipeSerializers.DATA_WIPE_SERIALIZER.get();
    }
}
```

### You

the right clicking on the machine with the blueprint still doesn't work, but the blueprint recipe data cleaning now works

### Gemini

That happens because returning `PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION` causes Minecraft to proceed to `useWithoutItem`, which opens the machine UI menu and ends the interaction pipeline before `BlueprintItem#useOn` can execute.

To fix this, change `PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION` to `SKIP_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION` in `MachineFrameworkBlock.java`. This skips the block interaction phase and lets the blueprint item handle the right click.

### Updated `useItemOn` in `MachineFrameworkBlock.java`

```java
    @Override
    protected @NotNull ItemInteractionResult useItemOn(@NotNull ItemStack stack, @NotNull BlockState state, Level level, @NotNull BlockPos pos, @NotNull Player player, @NotNull InteractionHand hand, @NotNull BlockHitResult hitResult) {
        // Skip default block interaction when holding a Blueprint so BlueprintItem#useOn executes
        if (stack.is(ModItems.BLUEPRINT.get())) {
            return ItemInteractionResult.SKIP_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION;
        }

        if (!level.isClientSide && player instanceof net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer serverPlayer) {
            BlockEntity blockEntity = level.getBlockEntity(pos);
            if (blockEntity instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity frameworkEntity) {
                if (stack.is(ModItems.YOOL.get())) {
                    level.playSound(null, pos, SoundEvents.LEVER_CLICK, net.minecraft.sounds.SoundSource.BLOCKS, 1.0F, 1.0F);
                    serverPlayer.openMenu(frameworkEntity, buf -> buf.writeBlockPos(pos));
                    return ItemInteractionResult.SUCCESS;
                }

                serverPlayer.openMenu(new MenuProvider() {
                    @Override
                    public net.minecraft.network.chat.@NotNull Component getDisplayName() {
                        return frameworkEntity.getDisplayName();
                    }

                    @Override
                    public AbstractContainerMenu createMenu(int containerId, @NotNull Inventory playerInventory, @NotNull Player player) {
                        return frameworkEntity.createInfoMenu(containerId, playerInventory, player);
                    }
                }, buf -> buf.writeBlockPos(pos));
                return ItemInteractionResult.SUCCESS;
            }
        }
        return ItemInteractionResult.PASS_TO_DEFAULT_BLOCK_INTERACTION;
    }
```

ok it works but with a caveat, actually 2

the machine mode screen won't update with the slots taken unless i enter config mode with the tool and then it shows the modules on the machine mode

the second one is... i do not want to store like... the process/progress of processing modules, that would make for some devolved gameplay loops

### Gemini

Those are two critical fixes, and your gameplay instincts are spot on. Storing processing progress or active internal states in a blueprint would lead to massive exploits or bizarre duplication loops.

Here is how we address both issues:

### 1. Fixing the UI Sync Issue (Client-Side Block Entity Sync)

When modules are pasted server-side via the blueprint, the client-side block entity instance does not automatically know its inventory changed until a sync packet or block update is triggered.

To fix this, we need to mark the block entity data as changed and send a block update to the client right after pasting.

### 2. Stripping Runtime / Processing Data (Clean Configuration)

When copying a module, we should explicitly filter out any transient runtime components (like internal progress, fuel ticks, or processing state data components) so that only permanent configuration data (like filters and face modes) is captured.

### Updated `BlueprintItem.java` Fixes

Replace your copy and paste methods in `BlueprintItem.java` with these clean versions:

```java
    private void copyMachineToBlueprint(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine, ItemStack blueprint, Player player) {
        ListTag slotList = new ListTag();
        int moduleCount = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < 27; i++) {
            ItemStack module = machine.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i);
            if (!module.isEmpty()) {
                moduleCount++;
                CompoundTag slotTag = new CompoundTag();
                slotTag.putInt("Slot", i);
                slotTag.putString("Item", BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.getKey(module.getItem()).toString());

                // Copy custom data but strip any runtime/processing progress state if present
                CustomData customData = module.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
                if (customData != null) {
                    CompoundTag tagCopy = customData.copyTag();
                    
                    // Prevent saving processing states/progress to avoid exploit loops
                    tagCopy.remove("Progress");
                    tagCopy.remove("BurnTime");
                    tagCopy.remove("CookTime");
                    
                    if (!tagCopy.isEmpty()) {
                        slotTag.put("CustomData", tagCopy);
                    }
                }

                slotList.add(slotTag);
            }
        }

        if (moduleCount == 0) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cCannot copy: Targeted machine framework is empty!"), true);
            return;
        }

        CustomData.update(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, blueprint, tag -> tag.put("BlueprintLayout", slotList));

        player.level().playSound(null, player.getX(), player.getY(), player.getZ(), SoundEvents.UI_CARTOGRAPHY_TABLE_TAKE_RESULT, SoundSource.PLAYERS, 0.8F, 1.2F);
        player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§aBlueprint copied! Recorded " + moduleCount + " modules."), true);
    }

    private void pasteBlueprintToMachine(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine, ItemStack blueprint, Player player) {
        CustomData customData = blueprint.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
        if (customData == null || !customData.copyTag().contains("BlueprintLayout")) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cBlueprint is blank! Shift + Right-Click a configured machine first."), true);
            return;
        }

        boolean hasModulesInstalled = false;
        for (int i = 0; i < 27; i++) {
            if (!machine.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i).isEmpty()) {
                hasModulesInstalled = true;
                break;
            }
        }

        if (hasModulesInstalled) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cTarget Machine Framework must be empty to apply a blueprint!"), true);
            return;
        }

        ListTag slotList = customData.copyTag().getList("BlueprintLayout", Tag.TAG_COMPOUND);
        if (slotList.isEmpty()) return;

        Map<Item, Integer> requiredModules = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
            CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
            ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
            Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);
            requiredModules.put(item, requiredModules.getOrDefault(item, 0) + 1);
        }

        if (!player.isCreative()) {
            Map<Item, Integer> availableCleanModules = countCleanModulesInInventory(player);

            for (Map.Entry<Item, Integer> entry : requiredModules.entrySet()) {
                Item requiredItem = entry.getKey();
                int neededCount = entry.getValue();
                int availableCount = availableCleanModules.getOrDefault(requiredItem, 0);

                if (availableCount < neededCount) {
                    String itemName = new ItemStack(requiredItem).getHoverName().getString();
                    player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cMissing modules: Needs " + neededCount + "x " + itemName + " (Clean)."), true);
                    return;
                }
            }
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
            CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
            int slotIndex = slotTag.getInt("Slot");
            ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
            Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);

            if (!player.isCreative()) {
                consumeCleanModule(player, item);
            }

            ItemStack newModuleStack = new ItemStack(item);
            if (slotTag.contains("CustomData")) {
                newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, CustomData.of(slotTag.getCompound("CustomData")));
                newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.MAX_STACK_SIZE, 1);
            }

            machine.getModuleHandler().setStackInSlot(slotIndex, newModuleStack);
        }

        // Force synchronization and state update so the UI updates instantly on the client screen
        machine.setChanged();
        Level level = machine.getLevel();
        if (level != null) {
            BlockState state = level.getBlockState(machine.getBlockPos());
            level.sendBlockUpdated(machine.getBlockPos(), state, state, 3);
        }

        player.level().playSound(null, machine.getBlockPos(), SoundEvents.ITEM_FRAME_ADD_ITEM, SoundSource.BLOCKS, 0.8F, 1.1F);
        player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§aBlueprint applied successfully!"), true);
    }
```

By calling `level.sendBlockUpdated(...)` alongside `machine.setChanged()`, the container state syncs to the client immediately, ensuring your modules show up in the machine UI without needing to open config mode first.

im pretty sure we defined a few of these as like... channels? i also have a few of these network classes, are those the ones we should use? or is just a client to server thing?

### Gemini

Those network classes in your `network` package (like `ServerboundToggleModuleDirectionPacket`, `ServerboundSetModuleConfigItemPacket`, etc.) are **client-to-server payload packets**. They are used when a player clicks a button or interacts with a UI element on the client side, telling the server to update the block entity data.

For applying blueprints, **no new packet classes are needed** because pasting happens entirely within `BlueprintItem#useOn`, which runs securely on the server side (`!level.isClientSide()`).

### Fixing the Two Remaining Issues

#### 1. Preventing Progress Data from Being Saved to Blueprints

To ensure blueprints never capture or restore transient processing states (like burn time or cooking progress), we ensure that any progress channel tags or NBT keys are fully scrubbed during the copy phase.

#### 2. Fixing the Machine UI Sync Issue

The reason the machine mode screen didn't update visually until you opened config mode is that the container menu state wasn't being re-synced to the client player.

### Updated `BlueprintItem.java` Implementation

Here is the clean, final version of `BlueprintItem.java` with both fixes implemented:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom;

import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents;
import net.minecraft.core.registries.BuiltInRegistries;
import net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag;
import net.minecraft.nbt.ListTag;
import net.minecraft.nbt.Tag;
import net.minecraft.network.chat.Component;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.sounds.SoundEvents;
import net.minecraft.sounds.SoundSource;
import net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult;
import net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player;
import net.minecraft.world.item.Item;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.item.TooltipFlag;
import net.minecraft.world.item.component.CustomData;
import net.minecraft.world.item.context.UseOnContext;
import net.minecraft.world.level.Level;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.HashMap;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;

public class BlueprintItem extends Item {

    public BlueprintItem(Properties properties) {
        super(properties);
    }

    @Override
    public @NotNull InteractionResult useOn(UseOnContext context) {
        Level level = context.getLevel();
        BlockPos pos = context.getClickedPos();
        Player player = context.getPlayer();
        ItemStack blueprintStack = context.getItemInHand();

        if (player == null) return InteractionResult.PASS;

        BlockEntity be = level.getBlockEntity(pos);
        if (!(be instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine)) {
            return InteractionResult.PASS;
        }

        if (!level.isClientSide()) {
            boolean isSneaking = player.isShiftKeyDown();

            if (isSneaking) {
                copyMachineToBlueprint(machine, blueprintStack, player);
            } else {
                pasteBlueprintToMachine(machine, blueprintStack, player);
            }
        }

        return InteractionResult.sidedSuccess(level.isClientSide());
    }

    private void copyMachineToBlueprint(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine, ItemStack blueprint, Player player) {
        ListTag slotList = new ListTag();
        int moduleCount = 0;

        for (int i = 0; i < 27; i++) {
            ItemStack module = machine.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i);
            if (!module.isEmpty()) {
                moduleCount++;
                CompoundTag slotTag = new CompoundTag();
                slotTag.putInt("Slot", i);
                slotTag.putString("Item", BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.getKey(module.getItem()).toString());

                CustomData customData = module.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
                if (customData != null) {
                    CompoundTag tagCopy = customData.copyTag();
                    
                    // Strip runtime processing progress and channel data to prevent gameplay exploits
                    tagCopy.remove("Progress");
                    tagCopy.remove("BurnTime");
                    tagCopy.remove("CookTime");
                    tagCopy.remove("ModuleChannels");

                    if (!tagCopy.isEmpty()) {
                        slotTag.put("CustomData", tagCopy);
                    }
                }

                slotList.add(slotTag);
            }
        }

        if (moduleCount == 0) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cCannot copy: Targeted machine framework is empty!"), true);
            return;
        }

        CustomData.update(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, blueprint, tag -> tag.put("BlueprintLayout", slotList));

        player.level().playSound(null, player.getX(), player.getY(), player.getZ(), SoundEvents.UI_CARTOGRAPHY_TABLE_TAKE_RESULT, SoundSource.PLAYERS, 0.8F, 1.2F);
        player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§aBlueprint copied! Recorded " + moduleCount + " modules."), true);
    }

    private void pasteBlueprintToMachine(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity machine, ItemStack blueprint, Player player) {
        CustomData customData = blueprint.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
        if (customData == null || !customData.copyTag().contains("BlueprintLayout")) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cBlueprint is blank! Shift + Right-Click a configured machine first."), true);
            return;
        }

        boolean hasModulesInstalled = false;
        for (int i = 0; i < 27; i++) {
            if (!machine.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i).isEmpty()) {
                hasModulesInstalled = true;
                break;
            }
        }

        if (hasModulesInstalled) {
            player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cTarget Machine Framework must be empty to apply a blueprint!"), true);
            return;
        }

        ListTag slotList = customData.copyTag().getList("BlueprintLayout", Tag.TAG_COMPOUND);
        if (slotList.isEmpty()) return;

        Map<Item, Integer> requiredModules = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
            CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
            ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
            Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);
            requiredModules.put(item, requiredModules.getOrDefault(item, 0) + 1);
        }

        if (!player.isCreative()) {
            Map<Item, Integer> availableCleanModules = countCleanModulesInInventory(player);

            for (Map.Entry<Item, Integer> entry : requiredModules.entrySet()) {
                Item requiredItem = entry.getKey();
                int neededCount = entry.getValue();
                int availableCount = availableCleanModules.getOrDefault(requiredItem, 0);

                if (availableCount < neededCount) {
                    String itemName = new ItemStack(requiredItem).getHoverName().getString();
                    player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§cMissing modules: Needs " + neededCount + "x " + itemName + " (Clean)."), true);
                    return;
                }
            }
        }

        for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
            CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
            int slotIndex = slotTag.getInt("Slot");
            ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
            Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);

            if (!player.isCreative()) {
                consumeCleanModule(player, item);
            }

            ItemStack newModuleStack = new ItemStack(item);
            if (slotTag.contains("CustomData")) {
                newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, CustomData.of(slotTag.getCompound("CustomData")));
                newModuleStack.set(DataComponents.MAX_STACK_SIZE, 1);
            }

            machine.getModuleHandler().setStackInSlot(slotIndex, newModuleStack);
        }

        // Force container synchronization so client UI menus update instantly without reopening
        machine.setChanged();
        Level level = machine.getLevel();
        if (level != null) {
            BlockState state = level.getBlockState(machine.getBlockPos());
            level.sendBlockUpdated(machine.getBlockPos(), state, state, 3);
            if (player instanceof net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer serverPlayer) {
                serverPlayer.containerMenu.broadcastChanges();
            }
        }

        player.level().playSound(null, machine.getBlockPos(), SoundEvents.ITEM_FRAME_ADD_ITEM, SoundSource.BLOCKS, 0.8F, 1.1F);
        player.displayClientMessage(Component.literal("§aBlueprint applied successfully!"), true);
    }

    private Map<Item, Integer> countCleanModulesInInventory(Player player) {
        Map<Item, Integer> cleanCounts = new HashMap<>();
        for (int i = 0; i < player.getInventory().getContainerSize(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = player.getInventory().getItem(i);
            if (!stack.isEmpty() && isCleanModule(stack)) {
                cleanCounts.put(stack.getItem(), cleanCounts.getOrDefault(stack.getItem(), 0) + stack.getCount());
            }
        }
        return cleanCounts;
    }

    private void consumeCleanModule(Player player, Item targetItem) {
        for (int i = 0; i < player.getInventory().getContainerSize(); i++) {
            ItemStack stack = player.getInventory().getItem(i);
            if (!stack.isEmpty() && stack.is(targetItem) && isCleanModule(stack)) {
                stack.shrink(1);
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    private boolean isCleanModule(ItemStack stack) {
        CustomData customData = stack.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
        return customData == null || customData.copyTag().isEmpty();
    }

    @Override
    public void appendHoverText(@NotNull ItemStack stack, Item.@NotNull TooltipContext context, @NotNull List<Component> tooltipComponents, @NotNull TooltipFlag tooltipFlag) {
        CustomData customData = stack.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
        if (customData != null && customData.copyTag().contains("BlueprintLayout")) {
            ListTag slotList = customData.copyTag().getList("BlueprintLayout", Tag.TAG_COMPOUND);

            Map<Item, Integer> summary = new HashMap<>();
            for (int i = 0; i < slotList.size(); i++) {
                CompoundTag slotTag = slotList.getCompound(i);
                ResourceLocation itemId = ResourceLocation.parse(slotTag.getString("Item"));
                Item item = BuiltInRegistries.ITEM.get(itemId);
                summary.put(item, summary.getOrDefault(item, 0) + 1);
            }

            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§7Stored Configuration:"));
            for (Map.Entry<Item, Integer> entry : summary.entrySet()) {
                String itemName = new ItemStack(entry.getKey()).getHoverName().getString();
                tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8 • §f" + entry.getValue() + "x §e" + itemName));
            }
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8Clear in crafting table to wipe data."));
        } else {
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§7Status: §cEmpty"));
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8Shift + Right-Click a machine to copy."));
        }

        super.appendHoverText(stack, context, tooltipComponents, tooltipFlag);
    }
}
```

Give this a spin in-game—pasting should now instantly update the main machine framework GUI view slots without requiring a config mode toggle, and all progress metadata is safely excluded from blueprints.

### Gemini

You understood the purpose of `ModuleChannels` correctly. `ModuleChannels` stores progress data on the module item stack whenever you extract that module from a machine framework, ensuring the progress persists on the item itself.

Hardcoding specific keys like `"ModuleChannels"`, `"BurnTime"`, or `"Progress"` directly inside `BlueprintItem` creates a maintenance bottleneck. Every time you or someone else adds a new processing module with unique runtime states, you would have to remember to update `BlueprintItem`.

Object-oriented design provides a cleaner solution. You can delegate data sanitization to the module items themselves by adding a method on `BaseModuleItem`. Each module type can define its own rules for what data gets copied to a blueprint.

### 1. Add a Method to `BaseModuleItem.java`

Provide a default implementation in `BaseModuleItem` that returns the custom data tag as-is for standard configurable modules:

```java
public CompoundTag getBlueprintData(ItemStack stack) {
    CustomData customData = stack.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
    if (customData == null) return null;
    return customData.copyTag();
}
```

### 2. Override the Method in `ProcessingModuleItem.java`

Processing modules override this method to strip out runtime progress keys automatically:

```java
@Override
public CompoundTag getBlueprintData(ItemStack stack) {
    CompoundTag tag = super.getBlueprintData(stack);
    if (tag != null) {
        tag.remove("Progress");
        tag.remove("BurnTime");
        tag.remove("CookTime");
        tag.remove("ModuleChannels");
    }
    return tag;
}
```

### 3. Simplify `BlueprintItem.java`

The blueprint copy logic becomes completely decoupled from specific module implementations. It simply calls the method on the module item:

```java
CustomData customData = module.get(DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
if (customData != null && module.getItem() instanceof BaseModuleItem baseModule) {
    CompoundTag cleanTag = baseModule.getBlueprintData(module);
    if (cleanTag != null && !cleanTag.isEmpty()) {
        slotTag.put("CustomData", cleanTag);
    }
}
```

### Why This Approach Works Best

- **Extensibility:** When you add a new processing module in the future, its class manages its own data rules. You touch only the new module class.
- **Consistency:** `BlueprintItem` remains generic, treating all modules through the unified `BaseModuleItem` interface contract.

That architectural direction is completely correct. Designing `ProcessingModuleItem` to act purely as a shared framework enabler allows concrete subclasses to manage their own unique recipes, progress metrics, and internal states.

### Separation of Concerns in Processing Modules

When processing modules encapsulate their own mechanics, `SmeltingModuleItem` owns its fuel consumption values, burn time tickers, and smelting recipe validation logic. Similarly, `ComposterModuleItem` owns its compost accumulation thresholds and data map integrations. The base `ProcessingModuleItem` class supplies the underlying infrastructure, providing standardized neighbor resolution routines, common overlay geometries, and shared click handling algorithms. This design pattern ensures that adding future processing mechanics requires writing code exclusively inside the new module class, maintaining clean boundaries across the entire system.

### Stonecutter Module Data Architecture

The stonecutter module operates without saving transient runtime progress. It stores configuration data limited strictly to its side orientation modes and its designated target item filter. Because it processes items instantaneously upon inventory ticks without accumulating intermediate progress ticks, it requires no progress channels in the block entity data array.

### Blueprint Serialization Behavior for Stonecutters

When a player creates a blueprint from a machine containing a stonecutter module, the blueprint serializes the item identifier, the face mode configurations, and the saved target item tag. When applied to another machine, the blueprint restores the target item filter and side modes instantly. Since no progress variables exist on the stonecutter module, the serialization process remains clean and lightweight.

### Gemini

Here is how your classes organize and how the data storage works across the machine entity and the items.

### 1. How the Class Files Are Structured

- **`BaseModuleItem`**: Handles universal module behavior, layout validation, and provides the base `getBlueprintData()` method.
- **`ProcessingModuleItem`**: Acts as the shared infrastructure enabler. It provides standard neighbor-slot resolution, side mode enums (Input, Output, Fuel, Disabled), rendering code for overlay buttons, and common click handlers.
- **`SmeltingModuleItem` & `ComposterModuleItem`**: Own their specific recipes, progress bars, fuel ticks, and how they map their internal mechanics to the machine entity channels.
- **`BlueprintItem`**: Remains completely generic. It simply calls `getBlueprintData()` on each module, letting individual modules strip out runtime states while keeping permanent configurations.

### 2. Where the Data Is Stored (The Split)

Data is split into two distinct categories depending on whether it is temporary runtime progress or permanent configuration:

#### **A. Runtime Progress Data (Stored in the Machine Entity)**

- **Where it lives:** While a machine is running, active progress (such as burn time, cook progress, or compost levels) lives inside the **`MachineFrameworkBlockEntity`** using its `moduleData[slot][channel]` integer grid.
- **What happens when removed:** When you extract a processing module out of a machine, `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity` serializes those active channels into the module item's NBT under `"ModuleChannels"` so you do not lose progress if you pick the module up.
- **Blueprints:** Blueprints explicitly strip `"ModuleChannels"` and progress timers during the copy phase so that blueprints never clone active item processing states.

#### **B. Configuration Data (Stored on the Module Item)**

- **Where it lives:** Permanent settings like side face modes, target item filters, and recipe locks live directly on the **Module Item's `CUSTOM_DATA` component**.
- **Blueprints:** Blueprints read this persistent configuration data and duplicate it across slots so you can paste exact setups onto fresh machines instantly.

It's a tough question, because players don't usually know which direction North is in the first place.

The dynamically-rearranging approach has the potential to be really confusing if a player is coming at it from a corner; they might think they're facing one way, when they're actually a few degrees off and facing another way. I could see a player opening the GUI, making a change, exiting, taking a step to the side, reopening the gui, and not realizing that all the squares have shifted one space over. Even better, use a textured border instead of a colored one; it's more legible to colorblind players, and you can use paired textures on opposite faces (e.g. circles on one side, circles and a thick bar on the other) to give players an additional clue about what's on the sides they can't see.

### 1. Cleaning Up the Tooltip Display

Printing raw Java map output in item tooltips creates clutter. You can replace that raw string representation with a clean, bulleted list by overriding `appendHoverText` in your `IoModuleItem` class.

Here is how you format the hover text for readability:

```java
@Override
public void appendHoverText(@NotNull ItemStack stack, Item.@NotNull TooltipContext context, @NotNull List<Component> tooltipComponents, @NotNull TooltipFlag tooltipFlag) {
    Map<Direction, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
    tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§7Face Configurations:"));
    
    for (Map.Entry<Direction, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
        String dirName = entry.getKey().getName();
        String capitalized = dirName.substring(0, 1).toUpperCase() + dirName.substring(1);
        FaceMode mode = entry.getValue();
        
        String colorCode = switch (mode) {
            case DISABLED -> "§8";
            case INPUT -> "§9";
            case OUTPUT -> "§c";
            case OPEN -> "§a";
        };
        
        tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8 • §f" + capitalized + ": " + colorCode + mode.name()));
    }

    super.appendHoverText(stack, context, tooltipComponents, tooltipFlag);
}
```

### 2. Solving the Side Configuration Dilemma

The feedback from your Reddit post highlights a genuine design challenge. Absolute compass directions force players to calculate global coordinates, while dynamic rotation creates disorientation when walking around the machine.

Industry standards across successful tech mods resolve this friction through specific design patterns:

- **Textured or Colored Block Faces:** Painting distinct icons or color borders on each exterior side of the machine block lets players look at the physical casing, identify the side instantly, and match it to the corresponding button in the interface.
- **Local Machine Frame Reference:** Structuring the GUI layout as a schematic cross view (Top, Bottom, Left, Right, Front, Back) anchored to the block itself gives players a spatial anchor point that remains constant regardless of where they stand.
- **Hover Tooltips on Buttons:** Hovering over individual direction buttons inside the GUI can display the exact global side name alongside its current state, giving immediate feedback without cluttering the main view.

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom;

import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;

public class IoModuleItem extends LogisticsModuleItem {

    public void renderModuleOverlay(GuiGraphics graphics, Slot slot, ItemStack stack, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity) {

                ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "textures/gui/container/io_module_overlay.png"),
                slot.x, slot.y,
                0.0f, 0.0f,
                16, 16,
                16, 16
        );
    }

    @Override
    public boolean isInsideOverlay(double mouseX, double mouseY, int slotX, int slotY) {
        // Extended bottom bound to cover the inventory overlap segment
        return mouseX >= slotX - 36 && mouseX <= slotX + 52 &&
                mouseY >= slotY - 18 && mouseY <= slotY + 38;
    }

    private Direction getIoClickedDirection(int slotX, int slotY, double mx, double my) {
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX, slotY)) return Direction.NORTH;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX, slotY - 18)) return Direction.UP;
        // Extended Down click detection range
        if (mx >= slotX && mx <= slotX + 16 && my >= slotY + 18 && my <= slotY + 38) return Direction.DOWN;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX - 18, slotY)) return Direction.WEST;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX + 18, slotY)) return Direction.EAST;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX + 36, slotY)) return Direction.SOUTH;
        return null;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean opensInlineOverlay() {
        return true; // IO modules use inline overlays
    }

    @Override
    public boolean shouldHideSlot(int configuringSlotIndex, int targetSlotIndex) {
        int row = configuringSlotIndex / 9;
        int col = configuringSlotIndex % 9;

        // IO Module overrides baseline to hide wider bounds for S and X buttons
        if (targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex) return true;
        if (row > 0 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 9) return true;
        if (row < 2 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 9) return true;
        if (col > 0 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 1) return true;
        if (col < 8 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 1) return true;
        if (col < 7 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 2) return true; // S button
        return col > 1 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 2; // X button
    }

    @Override
    public void renderCustomOverlay(GuiGraphics graphics, int slotX, int slotY, ItemStack stack, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font) {
        Map<Direction, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);

        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX, slotY, "N", modes.get(Direction.NORTH));
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX, slotY - 18, "U", modes.get(Direction.UP));
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX, slotY + 18, "D", modes.get(Direction.DOWN));
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX - 18, slotY, "W", modes.get(Direction.WEST));
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX + 18, slotY, "E", modes.get(Direction.EAST));
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX + 36, slotY, "S", modes.get(Direction.SOUTH));

        graphics.fill(slotX - 36, slotY, slotX - 20, slotY + 16, 0xFF8B0000);
        graphics.drawCenteredString(font, "X", slotX - 28, slotY + 4, 0xFFFFFF);
    }

    private void drawConfigButton(GuiGraphics graphics, net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font, int x, int y, String faceLabel, FaceMode mode) {
        graphics.fill(x, y, x + 16, y + 16, 0xFF888888);
        graphics.fill(x + 1, y + 1, x + 15, y + 15, mode.getColor());

        // Displays e.g., "N:T" or "U:F"
        graphics.drawCenteredString(font, faceLabel + ":" + mode.getLabelChar(), x + 8, y + 4, 0xFFFFFF);
    }

    @Override
    public void openConfiguration(ServerPlayer player, ItemStack moduleStack, int slotIndex, BlockPos blockPos) {
        // Client-side overlay handled via screen state
    }

    @Override
    public void handleCustomClick(double mouseX, double mouseY, int slotX, int slotY, ItemStack stack, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, net.minecraft.client.Minecraft minecraft) {
        Direction clickedDir = getIoClickedDirection(slotX, slotY, mouseX, mouseY);
        if (clickedDir != null) {
            if (minecraft.player != null) {
                minecraft.player.playNotifySound(SoundEvents.UI_BUTTON_CLICK.value(), net.minecraft.sounds.SoundSource.PLAYERS, 0.5F, 1.0F);
            }
            Map<Direction, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
            FaceMode nextMode = modes.get(clickedDir).next();
            setFaceMode(stack, clickedDir, nextMode);

            PacketDistributor.sendToServer(new ServerboundToggleIoFacePacket(slotIndex, clickedDir, blockEntity.getBlockPos()));
        }
    }

    private boolean isInside(double mx, double my, int x, int y) {
        return mx >= x && mx < x + 16 && my >= y && my < y + 16;
    }

    @Override
    public boolean isCloseButton(double mouseX, double mouseY, int slotX, int slotY) {
        return mouseX >= slotX - 36 && mouseX <= slotX - 20 && mouseY >= slotY && mouseY <= slotY + 16;
    }

    @Override
    public @Nullable net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable getItemHandlerForSide(
            net.minecraft.world.level.Level level,
            BlockPos pos,
            MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity,
            int slotIndex,
            ItemStack stack,
            Direction side) {
        Map<Direction, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        FaceMode mode = modes.get(side);

        if (mode == FaceMode.DISABLED) {
            return null;
        }

        int[] adjacentIndices = blockEntity.getAdjacentSlots(slotIndex);
        List<net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable> handlers = new ArrayList<>();

        for (int adj : adjacentIndices) {
            ItemStack adjModule = blockEntity.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(adj);
            if (adjModule.is(com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.ModItems.INVENTORY_MODULE.get())) {
                handlers.add(new FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler(blockEntity.getInventoryHandler(), adj, blockEntity, slotIndex));
            }
        }

        if (handlers.isEmpty()) {
            return null;
        }

        return new net.neoforged.neoforge.items.wrapper.CombinedInvWrapper(handlers.toArray(new net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable[0]));
    }

    public static class FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler extends com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.inventory.SingleSlotItemHandler {
        private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity;
        private final int ioModuleSlot;
        private final int targetSlot;

        public FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler(net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable itemHandler, int slot, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int ioModuleSlot) {
            super(itemHandler, slot);
            this.blockEntity = blockEntity;
            this.ioModuleSlot = ioModuleSlot;
            this.targetSlot = slot;
        }

        @Override
        public @NotNull ItemStack insertItem(int slot, @NotNull ItemStack stack, boolean simulate) {
            // Direct call to FilterModuleItem helper
            if (FilterModuleItem.isItemBlockedByFilters(blockEntity, ioModuleSlot, this.targetSlot, stack)) {
                return stack; // Rejected by filters!
            }
            return super.insertItem(slot, stack, simulate);
        }
    }

    public enum FaceMode {
        DISABLED(0, "D", 0xFF555555), // Dark gray
        INPUT(1, "I", 0xFF3366CC),    // Classic Blue
        OUTPUT(2, "O", 0xFFCC3333),   // Classic Red
        OPEN(3, "T", 0xFF00FFCC);     // Bright Cyan (Open/True bidirectional)

        private final int id;
        private final String labelChar;
        private final int color;

        FaceMode(int id, String labelChar, int color) {
            this.id = id;
            this.labelChar = labelChar;
            this.color = color;
        }

        public String getLabelChar() {
            return labelChar;
        }

        public int getColor() {
            return color;
        }

        public static FaceMode fromId(int id) {
            for (FaceMode mode : values()) {
                if (mode.id == id) return mode;
            }
            return DISABLED;
        }

        public FaceMode next() {
            return values()[(this.ordinal() + 1) % values().length];
        }
    }

    public static Map<Direction, FaceMode> getFaceModes(ItemStack stack) {
        Map<Direction, FaceMode> modes = new HashMap<>();
        CompoundTag facesTag = getCustomTag(stack, "FaceModes");
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            if (facesTag.contains(dir.getName())) {
                modes.put(dir, FaceMode.fromId(facesTag.getInt(dir.getName())));
            } else {
                modes.put(dir, FaceMode.DISABLED);
            }
        }
        return modes;
    }

    public static void setFaceMode(ItemStack stack, Direction direction, FaceMode mode) {
        modifyCustomData(stack, "FaceModes", facesTag -> facesTag.putInt(direction.getName(), mode.id));

        boolean hasConfig = getFaceModes(stack).values().stream().anyMatch(m -> m != FaceMode.DISABLED);
        updateStackSize(stack, hasConfig);
    }

    public static Set<Direction> getEnabledFaces(ItemStack stack) {
        Set<Direction> enabledFaces = EnumSet.noneOf(Direction.class);
        Map<Direction, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        for (Map.Entry<Direction, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
            if (entry.getValue() != FaceMode.DISABLED) {
                enabledFaces.add(entry.getKey());
            }
        }
        return enabledFaces;
    }

    @Override
    public void appendHoverText(@NotNull ItemStack stack, Item.@NotNull TooltipContext context, @NotNull List<Component> tooltipComponents, @NotNull TooltipFlag tooltipFlag) {
        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {
            Map<Direction, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§7Face Configurations:"));
            for (Map.Entry<Direction, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
                String dirName = entry.getKey().getName();
                String capitalized = dirName.substring(0, 1).toUpperCase() + dirName.substring(1);
                FaceMode mode = entry.getValue();

                String colorCode = switch (mode) {
                    case DISABLED -> "§8";
                    case INPUT -> "§9";
                    case OUTPUT -> "§c";
                    case OPEN -> "§a";
                };

                tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8 • §f" + capitalized + ": " + colorCode + mode.name()));
            }
        }
        super.appendHoverText(stack, context, tooltipComponents, tooltipFlag);
    }
}
```
