ok so the rule is... front is always relative to facing, left is right and right is left relative to facing, back is back relative to facing, the up texture has the front(facing) at the top of the sprite, same for the down texture

### Gemini

To handle that exact set of relative mapping rules, we can simplify the entire renderer.

Instead of drawing each face separately in world space, we can rotate the entire `PoseStack` once based on the machine's `FACING` direction. That makes `FRONT`, `BACK`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `UP`, and `DOWN` strictly relative to where the block is pointing.

Here is the breakdown of how the vertex UVs align with your rules:

1. **FRONT / BACK**: Rendered on the local Z faces.
2. **LEFT / RIGHT**: Flipped horizontally (swapping $U_0$ and $U_1$) so Left maps to the right visual side relative to facing, and vice versa.
3. **UP / DOWN**: Rendered on local Y faces with $V_0$ (top of the texture) pointing towards local North (which is `FRONT`).

Replace your **`MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`** with this exact implementation:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexConsumer;
import com.mojang.math.Axis;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.RelativeSide;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.custom.MachineFrameworkBlock;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.RenderType;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRendererProvider;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite;
import net.minecraft.core.Direction;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import org.joml.Matrix4f;

public class MachineFrameworkRenderer implements BlockEntityRenderer<MachineFrameworkBlockEntity> {

    private static final int FULL_BRIGHT = 15728880;

    public MachineFrameworkRenderer(BlockEntityRendererProvider.Context context) {
    }

    @Override
    public void render(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, float partialTick, PoseStack poseStack,
                       MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        BlockState state = blockEntity.getBlockState();
        Direction facing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        VertexConsumer consumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityTranslucent(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));

        poseStack.pushPose();

        // 1. Center transform origin
        poseStack.translate(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f);

        // 2. Rotate the ENTIRE local coordinate space to match the block's FACING
        // Facing NORTH = 0 deg, SOUTH = 180 deg, WEST = 90 deg, EAST = 270 deg
        float yRot = switch (facing) {
            case NORTH -> 0f;
            case SOUTH -> 180f;
            case WEST -> 90f;
            case EAST -> 270f;
            default -> 0f;
        };
        poseStack.mulPose(Axis.YP.rotationDegrees(yRot));

        // 3. Move back to min bounds (0.0 to 1.0 local space)
        poseStack.translate(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f);

        // Render all relative faces in local space
        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
            String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
            TextureAtlasSprite sprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));

            renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, sprite, side, 0, 229, 255, 255, packedOverlay);
        }

        poseStack.popPose();
    }

    private void renderRelativeFace(PoseStack poseStack, VertexConsumer consumer, TextureAtlasSprite sprite,
                                    RelativeSide side, int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, int packedOverlay) {
        Matrix4f matrix = poseStack.last().pose();

        float min = 0.0f;
        float max = 1.0f;
        float offset = 0.001f;

        float u0 = sprite.getU0();
        float u1 = sprite.getU1();
        float v0 = sprite.getV0();
        float v1 = sprite.getV1();

        switch (side) {
            case FRONT -> {
                // Local North (-Z) face
                float z = min - offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
            }
            case BACK -> {
                // Local South (+Z) face
                float z = max + offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            }
            case LEFT -> {
                // Local West (-X) face, flipped horizontal UVs (u1 to u0) to invert Left/Right
                float x = min - offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case RIGHT -> {
                // Local East (+X) face, flipped horizontal UVs (u1 to u0) to invert Left/Right
                float x = max + offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case UP -> {
                // Local Top (+Y) face: v0 (top of sprite) mapped to min Z (Local North / FRONT)
                float y = max + offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case DOWN -> {
                // Local Bottom (-Y) face: v0 (top of sprite) mapped to min Z (Local North / FRONT)
                float y = min - offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

### Quick Reference for Manual Edits

- **To swap Left and Right visually**: In `case LEFT` and `case RIGHT`, swap the pair of $X$ corner coordinates (`max` and `min`) passed into `addVertex`.
- **To rotate Top or Bottom 180 degrees**: In `case UP` or `case DOWN`, swap `(min, y, min)` with `(max, y, max)` on the vertex UV calls, or invert `v0`/`v1`.

### Gemini

Yes, you can animate both the color hue and the glow intensity dynamically every frame using the game time and partial ticks.

To create a smooth rainbow effect and a pulsing glow strength, you can calculate an HSB (Hue, Saturation, Brightness) color value where the hue shifts continuously based on time, and multiply the RGB channels by a sine wave to make the brightness pulse up and down.

Here is the updated **`MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`** file implementing both rainbow cycling and glow strength pulsing:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexConsumer;
import com.mojang.math.Axis;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.RelativeSide;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.custom.MachineFrameworkBlock;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.RenderType;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRendererProvider;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite;
import net.minecraft.core.Direction;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import org.joml.Matrix4f;

public class MachineFrameworkRenderer implements BlockEntityRenderer<MachineFrameworkBlockEntity> {

    private static final int FULL_BRIGHT = 15728880;

    public MachineFrameworkRenderer(BlockEntityRendererProvider.Context context) {
    }

    @Override
    public void render(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, float partialTick, PoseStack poseStack,
                       MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        BlockState state = blockEntity.getBlockState();
        Direction facing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        // Calculate continuous time for smooth animations
        long levelTime = blockEntity.getLevel() != null ? blockEntity.getLevel().getGameTime() : 0;
        float time = levelTime + partialTick;

        // Rainbow Hue cycling (adjust the multiplier 0.015f to change speed)
        float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
        int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
        int baseR = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF;
        int baseG = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF;
        int baseB = rgb & 0xFF;

        // Glow strength pulsing using a sine wave (ranges between 40% and 100% brightness)
        float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
        int red = (int) (baseR * pulse);
        int green = (int) (baseG * pulse);
        int blue = (int) (baseB * pulse);

        VertexConsumer consumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityTranslucent(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));

        poseStack.pushPose();

        poseStack.translate(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f);

        float yRot = switch (facing) {
            case NORTH -> 0f;
            case SOUTH -> 180f;
            case WEST -> 90f;
            case EAST -> 270f;
            default -> 0f;
        };
        poseStack.mulPose(Axis.YP.rotationDegrees(yRot));

        poseStack.translate(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f);

        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
            String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
            TextureAtlasSprite sprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));

            renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, sprite, side, red, green, blue, 255, packedOverlay);
        }

        poseStack.popPose();
    }

    private void renderRelativeFace(PoseStack poseStack, VertexConsumer consumer, TextureAtlasSprite sprite,
                                    RelativeSide side, int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, int packedOverlay) {
```

### Gemini

To make each face cycle through the colors independently, you can add a phase offset based on the index of each side. Calculating the hue and brightness pulse separately inside the loop for every individual face creates a wave effect where each side shifts through its colors at a different time.

Here is the updated **`MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`** file implementing dephased rainbow cycling and independent pulse timing per face:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexConsumer;
import com.mojang.math.Axis;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.RelativeSide;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.custom.MachineFrameworkBlock;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.RenderType;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRendererProvider;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite;
import net.minecraft.core.Direction;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import org.joml.Matrix4f;

public class MachineFrameworkRenderer implements BlockEntityRenderer<MachineFrameworkBlockEntity> {

    private static final int FULL_BRIGHT = 15728880;

    public MachineFrameworkRenderer(BlockEntityRendererProvider.Context context) {
    }

    @Override
    public void render(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, float partialTick, PoseStack poseStack,
                       MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        BlockState state = blockEntity.getBlockState();
        Direction facing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        long levelTime = blockEntity.getLevel() != null ? blockEntity.getLevel().getGameTime() : 0;
        float time = levelTime + partialTick;

        // Base global time hue for overall shifting speed
        float baseHue = time * 0.015f;

        VertexConsumer consumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityTranslucent(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));

        poseStack.pushPose();

        poseStack.translate(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f);

        float yRot = switch (facing) {
            case NORTH -> 0f;
            case SOUTH -> 180f;
            case WEST -> 90f;
            case EAST -> 270f;
            default -> 0f;
        };
        poseStack.mulPose(Axis.YP.rotationDegrees(yRot));

        poseStack.translate(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f);

        // Loop through each side and calculate unique dephased colors
        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
            int sideIndex = side.ordinal();

            // Add a phase offset per face index so they do not sync up
            float faceHue = (baseHue + (sideIndex * 0.16f)) % 1.0f;
            int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(faceHue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
            int baseR = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF;
            int baseG = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF;
            int baseB = rgb & 0xFF;

            // Offset the sine wave phase for independent brightness pulsing
            float facePulse = (float) (Math.sin((time * 0.1) + (sideIndex * 1.2f)) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
            int red = (int) (baseR * facePulse);
            int green = (int) (baseG * facePulse);
            int blue = (int) (baseB * facePulse);

            String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
            TextureAtlasSprite sprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));

            renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, sprite, side, red, green, blue, 255, packedOverlay);
        }

        poseStack.popPose();
    }

    private void renderRelativeFace(PoseStack poseStack, VertexConsumer consumer, TextureAtlasSprite sprite,
                                    RelativeSide side, int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, int packedOverlay) {
        Matrix4f matrix = poseStack.last().pose();

        float min = 0.0f;
        float max = 1.0f;
        float offset = 0.001f;

        float u0 = sprite.getU0();
        float u1 = sprite.getU1();
        float v0 = sprite.getV0();
        float v1 = sprite.getV1();

        switch (side) {
            case FRONT -> {
                float z = min - offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
            }
            case BACK -> {
                float z = max + offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            }
            case LEFT -> {
                float x = min - offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case RIGHT -> {
                float x = max + offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case UP -> {
                float y = max + offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case DOWN -> {
                float y = min - offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
```

### Gemini

That makes total sense. Having each face out of sync turns it into a chaotic disco block rather than a unified machine.

To fix this, calculate the rainbow hue and pulse intensity **once** outside the loop so that every face shares the exact same color and brightness pulse simultaneously.

### Updated `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`

```java

    }

                       MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
        int baseR = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF;
        int baseG = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF;
        int baseB = rgb & 0xFF;

        // Calculate a single unified pulse intensity for all faces

        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
```

### You

now the brightness is desync

### Gemini

The uneven brightness happens because Minecraft applies diffuse lighting shading to entity vertex normals based on the direction each face points, which darkens certain sides even when full light is applied.

Switching the render type to **`RenderType.entityTranslucentEmissive`** disables diffuse lighting shading completely, ensuring every face renders at uniform full brightness.

```java
    @Override

                       MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        BlockState state = blockEntity.getBlockState();
        Direction facing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        long levelTime = blockEntity.getLevel() != null ? blockEntity.getLevel().getGameTime() : 0;
        float time = levelTime + partialTick;

        float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
        int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
        int baseR = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF;
        int baseG = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF;
        int baseB = rgb & 0xFF;

        float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
        int red = (int) (baseR * pulse);
        int green = (int) (baseG * pulse);
        int blue = (int) (baseB * pulse);

        // Use entityTranslucentEmissive to ignore diffuse lighting shadows across different faces
        VertexConsumer consumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityTranslucentEmissive(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));

        poseStack.pushPose();

        poseStack.translate(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f);

        float yRot = switch (facing) {
            case NORTH -> 0f;
            case SOUTH -> 180f;
            case WEST -> 90f;
            case EAST -> 270f;
            default -> 0f;

        poseStack.mulPose(Axis.YP.rotationDegrees(yRot));

        poseStack.translate(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f);

                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));
```

### You

is it possible to add emissive textures to items asides from blocks?

### Gemini

Yes, you can add emissive textures to items.

You can implement this using two primary methods depending on your workflow:

### 1. Code-Based Custom Item Renderer (BEWLR)

You can create a custom item renderer by implementing a `BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer` (BEWLR) and registering it via NeoForge's `ClientItemExtensions`.

- Inside your item renderer class, you use `RenderType.entityTranslucentEmissive(...)` exactly like your block entity renderer.
- This allows you to render animated sprites, apply dynamic color tinting, and handle pulsing rainbow effects for item models held in hands or dropped on the ground.

### 2. Resource Pack Emissive Textures

If you prefer a resource pack solution without writing custom Java code, you can use texture feature mods like Continuity.

- You place a `.properties` file next to your item texture inside your resource pack.
- The properties file specifies the target item texture and enables emissive rendering automatically when loaded in the game.

### Gemini

That makes complete sense. When multiple modules interact with the same face, you need a deterministic priority system to resolve conflicts so the visual indicators and automation rules behave predictably.

To implement this second layer of emissive textures cleanly, you can break the solution down into two parts: **priority aggregation** inside the block entity and **layered rendering** with depth offsets inside the renderer to prevent Z-fighting between the base glow layer and the IO status layer.

### Step 1: Add Priority Resolution in `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity`

Add a method to evaluate all installed `IoModuleItem` slots in the machine and combine their face modes according to your priority hierarchy (`OPEN` > `OUTPUT` / `INPUT` > `DISABLED`).

Open your **`MachineFrameworkBlockEntity.java`** file and add these methods:

```java
public IoModuleItem.FaceMode getEffectiveFaceMode(RelativeSide side) {
    IoModuleItem.FaceMode resolvedMode = IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED;

    // Iterate through all module slots in the inventory handler
    for (int i = 0; i < this.getModuleHandler().getSlots(); i++) {
        ItemStack stack = this.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i);
        if (stack.getItem() instanceof com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom.IoModuleItem) {
            Map<RelativeSide, IoModuleItem.FaceMode> modes = com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom.IoModuleItem.getFaceModes(stack);
            IoModuleItem.FaceMode mode = modes.get(side);

            if (mode == null || mode == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED) {
                continue;
            }

            resolvedMode = combineFaceModes(resolvedMode, mode);
        }
    }
    return resolvedMode;
}

private IoModuleItem.FaceMode combineFaceModes(IoModuleItem.FaceMode current, IoModuleItem.FaceMode incoming) {
    // OPEN (Full Input/Output) has the highest priority and overrides other states
    if (current == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN || incoming == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN) {
        return IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN;
    }
    // Combining input and output across different modules upgrades the face mode to OPEN
    if ((current == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.INPUT && incoming == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OUTPUT) ||
        (current == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OUTPUT && incoming == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.INPUT)) {
        return IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN;
    }
    // Take the higher ordinal mode if priority matches
    return incoming.ordinal() > current.ordinal() ? incoming : current;
}
```

```java
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case DOWN -> {
                float y = min - offset;
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);

                consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
            }

}
```

### Gemini

Your instinct is entirely correct. Keeping the block entity clean and agnostic of specific item classes is much better architecture. Pushing the responsibility down into the modules through polymorphism means the block entity only needs to talk to `BaseModuleItem`, letting each module manage its own behavior.

You can completely remove any direct mentions of `IoModuleItem` from **`MachineFrameworkBlockEntity.java`** by leveraging virtual methods on `BaseModuleItem`.

Here is how to clean it up step by step.

### Step 1: Add a Face Mode Hook to `BaseModuleItem`

Add a default method in your base module class that returns an empty map, allowing any module type to optionally contribute face configurations without forcing other modules to care:

```java
public Map<RelativeSide, IoModuleItem.FaceMode> getFaceModes(ItemStack stack) {
    return Collections.emptyMap();
}
```

### Step 2: Handle IO Ticking Inside `IoModuleItem`

Since `BaseModuleItem` already has a `tickModule` method called during the server tick, you can move the item pushing and pulling logic directly into **`IoModuleItem.java`**:

```java
@Override
public void tickModule(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
    // Run item automation every 10 ticks
    if (level.getGameTime() % 10 != 0) return;

    BlockState state = level.getBlockState(pos);
    Direction machineFacing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            : Direction.NORTH;

    Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
    for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
        Direction worldDir = entry.getKey().toWorldDirection(machineFacing);
        if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.OUTPUT) {
            blockEntity.pushItemsToSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
        } else if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.INPUT) {
            blockEntity.pullItemsFromSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
        }
    }
}
```

*(Note: Make sure `pushItemsToSide` and `pullItemsFromSide` in `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity` are package-private so `IoModuleItem` can call them).*

### Step 3: Streamline `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity.java`

With those responsibilities moved to the modules, `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity` no longer needs to check for `IoModuleItem` instances.

Replace your `serverTick` and add the clean polymorphic face resolver in **`MachineFrameworkBlockEntity.java`**:

```java
public IoModuleItem.FaceMode getEffectiveFaceMode(RelativeSide side) {
    IoModuleItem.FaceMode resolvedMode = IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED;

    for (int i = 0; i < this.getModuleHandler().getSlots(); i++) {
        ItemStack stack = this.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(i);
        if (stack.getItem() instanceof BaseModuleItem baseModule) {
            Map<RelativeSide, IoModuleItem.FaceMode> modes = baseModule.getFaceModes(stack);
            IoModuleItem.FaceMode mode = modes.get(side);

            if (mode == null || mode == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED) {
                continue;
            }

            resolvedMode = combineFaceModes(resolvedMode, mode);
        }
    }
    return resolvedMode;
}

private IoModuleItem.FaceMode combineFaceModes(IoModuleItem.FaceMode current, IoModuleItem.FaceMode incoming) {
    if (current == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN || incoming == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN) {
        return IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN;
    }
    if ((current == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.INPUT && incoming == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OUTPUT) ||
        (current == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OUTPUT && incoming == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.INPUT)) {
        return IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN;
    }
    return incoming.ordinal() > current.ordinal() ? incoming : current;
}

public static void serverTick(
        net.minecraft.world.level.Level level,
        BlockPos blockPos,
        BlockState state,
        MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity
) {
    if (level.isClientSide()) return;

    // Every module handles its own tick behavior polymorphically
    for (int i = 0; i < blockEntity.moduleHandler.getSlots(); i++) {
        ItemStack moduleStack = blockEntity.moduleHandler.getStackInSlot(i);
        if (moduleStack.getItem() instanceof BaseModuleItem baseModule) {
            baseModule.tickModule((net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel) level, blockEntity.getBlockPos(), blockEntity, i, moduleStack);
        }
    }
}
```

This keeps your block entity lightweight, delegates item-specific logic directly to the items where it belongs, and makes adding future module types modular and clean.

```java
public static void handle(ServerboundToggleIoFacePacket packet, IPayloadContext context) {
    context.enqueueWork(() -> {
        ServerPlayer player = (ServerPlayer) context.player();
        if (player.level().getBlockEntity(packet.blockPos()) instanceof MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity) {
            ItemStack stack = blockEntity.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(packet.slotIndex());
            if (stack.getItem() instanceof BaseModuleItem module) {
                Map<RelativeSide, IoModuleItem.FaceMode> modes = module.getFaceModes(stack);
                IoModuleItem.FaceMode currentMode = modes.get(packet.relativeSide());
                IoModuleItem.FaceMode nextMode = currentMode.next();
                IoModuleItem.setFaceMode(stack, packet.relativeSide(), nextMode);
                blockEntity.setChanged();
            }
        }
    });
}
```

```java
public static void setFaceMode(ItemStack stack, RelativeSide side, FaceMode mode) {

}
```

```java
/**
 * Pulls items from an external inventory into adjacent inventory modules.
 */
void pullItemsFromSide(int moduleSlot, Direction side) {
    if (level == null) return;

    int[] adjacentIndices = getAdjacentSlots(moduleSlot);
    for (int adj : adjacentIndices) {
        ItemStack adjModule = moduleHandler.getStackInSlot(adj);

        if (adjModule.is(ModItems.INVENTORY_MODULE.get())) {
            BlockPos sourcePos = worldPosition.relative(side);
            IItemHandler sourceHandler = level.getCapability(
                    net.neoforged.neoforge.capabilities.Capabilities.ItemHandler.BLOCK,
                    sourcePos,
                    side.getOpposite()
            );

            if (sourceHandler != null) {
                IItemHandler targetHandler = new SingleSlotItemHandler(inventoryHandler, adj);
                transferItems(sourceHandler, targetHandler, moduleSlot, adj);
            }
        }
    }
}

/**

    for (int adj : adjacentIndices) {

                    targetPos,
                    side.getOpposite()
            );

            if (targetHandler != null) {
                transferItems(sourceHandler, targetHandler, moduleSlot, adj);
            }
        }
    }
}
```

```java
    TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
            .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));
    
    int colorInt = faceMode.getColor();
    int ioR = (colorInt >> 16) & 0xFF;
    int ioG = (colorInt >> 8) & 0xFF;
    int ioB = colorInt & 0xFF;

    renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, ioSprite, side, 0.002f, ioR, ioG, ioB, 255, packedOverlay);
}
```

This approach requires only a single texture asset while allowing each mode to display its unique color automatically.

Place the second layer rendering code directly inside the **`render(...)` method**, right inside the `for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values())` loop *after* it draws the base rainbow glow layer.

Here is how your loop inside the `render` method should look to handle both layers cleanly:

```java
for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
    String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
    
    // 1. Layer 1: Base Rainbow Glow Texture
    TextureAtlasSprite baseSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
            .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));
    renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, baseSprite, side, red, green, blue, 255, packedOverlay);

    // 2. Layer 2: IO Module Status Overlay Texture
    IoModuleItem.FaceMode faceMode = blockEntity.getEffectiveFaceMode(side);
    if (faceMode != IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED) {
        TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));
        
        int colorInt = faceMode.getColor();
        int ioR = (colorInt >> 16) & 0xFF;
        int ioG = (colorInt >> 8) & 0xFF;
        int ioB = colorInt & 0xFF;

        // Note: You will need to adjust renderRelativeFace or pass a custom offset (0.002f) 
        // to prevent Z-fighting against the base layer.
        renderIoOverlayFace(poseStack, consumer, ioSprite, side, 0.002f, ioR, ioG, ioB, 255, packedOverlay);
```

there's one error with this method, where are you recalling it from?

### Gemini

That error happens because `renderIoOverlayFace` was just a placeholder name. Instead of creating a separate method, you can update your existing `renderRelativeFace` method to accept an explicit `offset` parameter.

This lets you reuse the exact same method for both layers by passing `0.001f` for the base glow and `0.002f` for the IO status overlay.

### Update `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`

Modify your `render` loop and update `renderRelativeFace` to accept the offset parameter:

```java
@Override
public void render(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, float partialTick, PoseStack poseStack,
                   MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

    BlockState state = blockEntity.getBlockState();
    Direction facing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            : Direction.NORTH;

    long levelTime = blockEntity.getLevel() != null ? blockEntity.getLevel().getGameTime() : 0;
    float time = levelTime + partialTick;

    float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
    int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
    int baseR = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF;
    int baseG = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF;
    int baseB = rgb & 0xFF;

    float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
    int red = (int) (baseR * pulse);
    int green = (int) (baseG * pulse);
    int blue = (int) (baseB * pulse);

    VertexConsumer consumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityTranslucentEmissive(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));

    poseStack.pushPose();

    poseStack.translate(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f);

    float yRot = switch (facing) {
        case NORTH -> 0f;
        case SOUTH -> 180f;
        case WEST -> 90f;
        case EAST -> 270f;
        default -> 0f;
    };
    poseStack.mulPose(Axis.YP.rotationDegrees(yRot));

    poseStack.translate(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f);

    for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
        String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
        
        // 1. Layer 1: Base Rainbow Glow Texture
        TextureAtlasSprite baseSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));
        renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, baseSprite, side, 0.001f, red, green, blue, 255, packedOverlay);

        // 2. Layer 2: IO Module Status Overlay Texture
        IoModuleItem.FaceMode faceMode = blockEntity.getEffectiveFaceMode(side);
        if (faceMode != IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED) {
            TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));
            
            int colorInt = faceMode.getColor();
            int ioR = (colorInt >> 16) & 0xFF;
            int ioG = (colorInt >> 8) & 0xFF;
            int ioB = colorInt & 0xFF;

            renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, ioSprite, side, 0.002f, ioR, ioG, ioB, 255, packedOverlay);
        }
    }

    poseStack.popPose();
}

private void renderRelativeFace(PoseStack poseStack, VertexConsumer consumer, TextureAtlasSprite sprite,
                                RelativeSide side, float offset, int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, int packedOverlay) {
    Matrix4f matrix = poseStack.last().pose();

    float min = 0.0f;
    float max = 1.0f;

    float u0 = sprite.getU0();
    float u1 = sprite.getU1();
    float v0 = sprite.getV0();
    float v1 = sprite.getV1();

    switch (side) {
        case FRONT -> {
            float z = min - offset;
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
        }
        case BACK -> {
            float z = max + offset;
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, max, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, min, z).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
        }
        case LEFT -> {
            float x = min - offset;
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(-1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
        }
        case RIGHT -> {
            float x = max + offset;
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, max, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, min, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setNormal(1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
        }
        case UP -> {
            float y = max + offset;
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
        }
        case DOWN -> {
            float y = min - offset;
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, max).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v0).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, max, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u1, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
            consumer.addVertex(matrix, min, y, min).setColor(red, green, blue, alpha).setUv(u0, v1).setOverlay(packedOverlay).setLight(FULL_BRIGHT).setNormal(0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
        }
    }
}
```

```java
private void vertex(VertexConsumer consumer, Matrix4f matrix, float x, float y, float z, int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, float u, float v, int overlay, int light, float normalX, float normalY, float normalZ) {
    consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, y, z)
            .setColor(red, green, blue, alpha)
            .setUv(u, v)
            .setOverlay(overlay)
            .setLight(light)
            .setNormal(normalX, normalY, normalZ);
}
```

```java
    float min = 0.0f;

    float u0 = sprite.getU0();
    float u1 = sprite.getU1();

        }
        case LEFT -> {
            float x = min - offset;
            vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);

        }
        case RIGHT -> {
            float x = max + offset;
            vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
```

### Gemini

The feeling of inconsistency usually comes from the mental friction between **2D GUI grid coordinates** (up, down, left, right in your 3×9 screen) and **3D world directions** (North, South, East, West relative to the machine's facing). When the machine rotates in the world, a "Left" side in the GUI maps to a different world vector, which can make automation feel unpredictable if not anchored to a solid design rule.

To make this feel completely intuitive and match what players expect from advanced tech mods, the cleanest design model relies on these core rules:

### 1. The Pipeline Rule (Adjacency = Connection)

- **Inventory Modules** act as internal buffers or storage bins.
- **IO Modules** act as the bridge to the outside world.
- **Adjacency in the GUI grid** links them. If an IO module is directly touching an Inventory module (above, below, left, or right in the grid), that IO module handles input/output specifically for that inventory slot.

### 2. Directional Independence (No Conflicts)

If one inventory slot touches two different IO modules (e.g., an Input on the left and an Output on the right), **they should never conflict**:

- **Input IO Module:** Strictly pulls items *from* its configured world side *into* the connected inventory slot.
- **Output IO Module:** Strictly pushes items *from* the connected inventory slot *out* to its configured world side.
- Because one only pulls and the other only pushes, they form a natural throughput pipeline (external chest $\rightarrow$ machine $\rightarrow$ output pipe) without blocking each other.

### 3. Deterministic Tick Order

To ensure behavior is 100% consistent and doesn't fluctuate frame-by-frame, make sure your block entity ticks module slots in a fixed, predictable sequence (e.g., iterating cleanly from slot `0` to `26`). This prevents race conditions where automation order depends on hash map iteration or random sorting.

what if both io modules input and output respectively to the same face? right now it's like a 50/50 if it pushes to the inventory or if it pulls to the machine

### Gemini

That unpredictable behavior happens because of a race condition in the server tick loop. When an input module and an output module target the same face or inventory slot at the same time, they execute in whatever order the module slots are indexed. One tick the input runs first and pulls an item in, and the next tick the output might run first and push it right back out. This creates a constant bouncing effect.

To make the behavior feel completely intuitive and reliable like standard tech mods, you can establish three clear design rules for your automation pipeline:

### 1. Enforce a Strict Execution Order

Instead of letting module slots tick in arbitrary order, separate the server tick into two distinct phases across all modules:

- **Phase One (Imports):** Process every active input module across the machine first. This pulls raw materials into the internal inventory slots.
- **Phase Two (Exports):** Process every active output module second. This pushes finished or excess items out to external inventories.

Running all inputs before any outputs ensures that items always flow inward, get processed, and then flow outward in a predictable sequence.

### 2. Define Strict Role Separation

An input module and an output module on the same face should have distinct responsibilities:

- **Input Modules** should only pull items that match valid input criteria or pass through your filter modules.
- **Output Modules** should only push items that are marked as finished products or excess stock.

### 3. Leverage Your Existing Filter Modules

Since you already built a robust filtering system with `FilterModuleItem`, players can pair an inventory module with a filter to restrict what the output side is allowed to touch. If an output slot is restricted to only push non-ingredient items, it will never steal the raw materials that the input module just pulled in.

Updating your tick dispatcher in `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity` to handle all pull operations before push operations will instantly eliminate the random fifty-fifty bouncing behavior.

### Gemini

The root cause of that 50/50 behavior is how `tickModule` is currently structured in `IoModuleItem.java`.

Right now, when `IoModuleItem.tickModule` runs, it iterates through its configured faces and immediately calls `pullItemsFromSide` or `pushItemsToSide` on the spot. Since `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity.serverTick` iterates through module slots `0` to `26` sequentially, whichever IO module sits in a lower slot index runs first. If your Output module is in slot 2 and your Input module is in slot 5, Output always steals the items first; if you swap their slot positions, Input runs first instead.

Here is the exact clean solution to make IO execution deterministic, pipeline-aligned, and rock solid across your framework:

### 1. Separate Input and Output Ticking in `IoModuleItem.java`

Replace the inline push/pull execution inside `tickModule` with explicit pass-based execution methods:

```java
@Override
public void tickModule(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
    // Left empty intentionally: automation is now handled via explicit framework pass execution
}

public void tickInputs(Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
    if (level.isClientSide()) return;

    BlockState state = level.getBlockState(pos);
    Direction machineFacing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            : Direction.NORTH;

    Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
    for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
        if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.INPUT) {
            Direction worldDir = entry.getKey().toWorldDirection(machineFacing);
            blockEntity.pullItemsFromSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
        }
    }
}

public void tickOutputs(Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
    if (level.isClientSide()) return;

    BlockState state = level.getBlockState(pos);
    Direction machineFacing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
            : Direction.NORTH;

    Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
    for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
        if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.OUTPUT) {
            Direction worldDir = entry.getKey().toWorldDirection(machineFacing);
            blockEntity.pushItemsToSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. Implement a 3-Phase Server Tick in `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity.java`

Update `serverTick` in `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity.java` to run all inputs first, process work second, and push outputs last:

```java
public static void serverTick(
        net.minecraft.world.level.Level level,
        BlockPos blockPos,
        BlockState state,
        MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity
) {
    if (level.isClientSide()) return;

    // Phase 1: Pull external items into internal inventory modules
    for (int i = 0; i < blockEntity.moduleHandler.getSlots(); i++) {
        ItemStack moduleStack = blockEntity.moduleHandler.getStackInSlot(i);
        if (moduleStack.getItem() instanceof IoModuleItem ioModule) {
            ioModule.tickInputs(level, blockPos, blockEntity, i, moduleStack);
        }
    }

    // Phase 2: Processing modules process recipes / work on internal inventories
    for (int i = 0; i < blockEntity.moduleHandler.getSlots(); i++) {
        ItemStack moduleStack = blockEntity.moduleHandler.getStackInSlot(i);
        if (moduleStack.getItem() instanceof com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom.ProcessingModuleItem processingModule) {
            processingModule.tickModule(level, blockPos, blockEntity, i, moduleStack);
        }
    }

    // Phase 3: Push processed or finished items out to external inventories
    for (int i = 0; i < blockEntity.moduleHandler.getSlots(); i++) {
        ItemStack moduleStack = blockEntity.moduleHandler.getStackInSlot(i);
        if (moduleStack.getItem() instanceof IoModuleItem ioModule) {
            ioModule.tickOutputs(level, blockPos, blockEntity, i, moduleStack);
        }
    }
}
```

### Why this fixes it completely

1. **No Slot Index Bias:** Slot 0 vs Slot 20 no longer causes race conditions.
2. **Guaranteed Automation Flow:** Raw materials arrive in Phase 1, machines craft in Phase 2, products leave in Phase 3.
3. **No Item Bouncing:** Items will never be pulled and immediately pushed back out in the exact same tick frame.

### Gemini

Yes, **that completely makes sense** based on how the automation pipeline is structured.

### Why This Happens

During **Phase 3 (`tickOutputs`)**, the machine checks every inventory slot connected to an IO module configured as `OUTPUT` (or `OPEN`). If it finds an item sitting in that inventory slot, its job is to immediately export it to the external world.

If a hopper or an external pipe pushes raw items into that slot, the machine's auto-output loop sees items in the slot and immediately pushes them right back out.

### The Underlying Design Logic

In modular machine systems, this behavior is actually working as intended, but it highlights a fundamental rule of machine automation: **Slot Segregation**.

- **Input Buffers** should only be touched by Input IO modules or input pipes, holding incoming raw materials.
- **Output Buffers** should only be touched by Output IO modules or extraction pipes, holding finished products.

If an inventory slot is tied to an **Output** face/module, the machine treats it strictly as an exit door. If raw ingredients end up there, the machine assumes they are ready to be expelled.

### How to Keep It Intuitive

To prevent output slots from spitting out raw inputs, players (and your mod's design pattern) handle this in a couple of standard ways:

1. **Grid Separation:** Players dedicate specific inventory modules in the 3x9 grid purely for inputs (serviced by input IO modules) and separate inventory modules for outputs (serviced by output IO modules).
2. **Filter Modules:** Pairing an output inventory slot with a **Filter Module** ensures that the output side can only push out crafted items or processed products, completely ignoring raw ingredients even if they end up in the same slot.

When you're back at it tomorrow, keeping your input and output inventories partitioned in the grid will instantly solve that tug-of-war!

hmm the color is incorrect then, cuz... this cyan is like when it's open, but if there's both input and output onto the same face and in the same slot it acts more like an output... is it possible to cycle 2 different colors on that face when it's the case?

### Gemini

Yes, cycling colors on that face is fully possible. When the resolved mode is `OPEN` (meaning both input and output are active on that face), you can interpolate the color between blue and red over time using the existing `time` variable in your renderer.

### How to Implement Color Cycling

You can check if `faceMode` is `FaceMode.OPEN` and calculate a smoothly pulsing color transition between the input blue and output red values.

Update the color extraction block inside your renderer loop in `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`:

```java
int colorInt = faceMode.getColor();
int ioR, ioG, ioB;

if (faceMode == FaceMode.OPEN) {
    // Smoothly cycle between Input Blue and Output Red using a sine wave
    float cycle = (float) ((Math.sin(time * 0.15f) + 1.0f) * 0.5f);
    
    int inputR = 0x33, inputG = 0x66, inputB = 0xCC;
    int outputR = 0xCC, outputG = 0x33, outputB = 0x33;
    
    ioR = (int) (inputR + (outputR - inputR) * cycle);
    ioG = (int) (inputG + (outputG - inputG) * cycle);
    ioB = (int) (inputB + (outputB - inputB) * cycle);
} else {
    ioR = (colorInt >> 16) & 0xFF;
    ioG = (colorInt >> 8) & 0xFF;
    ioB = colorInt & 0xFF;
}
```

This approach keeps cyan reserved for other potential shared states while giving dual input and output faces a dynamic visual indicator that clearly communicates both active roles at once.

Your modular system creates a rich combination space depending on whether you look at an individual module or the entire machine framework.

Here is the exact breakdown of the possible states and situations in your system:

### 1. Per Face on a Single IO Module

An individual IO module has 6 relative sides (`FRONT`, `BACK`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`, `UP`, `DOWN`). Each side independently supports 4 possible states (`DISABLED`, `INPUT`, `OUTPUT`, `OPEN`).

- This creates $4^6$, which equals **4,096 unique configuration states** for a single IO module item.

### 2. Resolved Operational States on Any World Face

When multiple modules in your 27-slot grid overlap on the same external world face, your `combineFaceModes` method evaluates them into **4 effective operational states**:

1. **Disabled**: The face remains completely inactive. No automated item transfers occur.
2. **Input**: The face acts strictly as an intake channel. Items flow inward from external inventories into internal buffers.
3. **Output**: The face acts strictly as an exhaust channel. Items flow outward from internal inventories to external pipes or containers.
4. **Open (Dual Flow)**: Both input and output roles merge on that face. This handles simultaneous bidirectional movement or throughput setups.

### 3. Full Machine Framework Scale

With 27 available slots in the grid, players can combine inventory modules, processing modules, filter modules, and multiple IO modules in countless layouts. While the exact total permutation count scales into millions of possible item arrangements, every setup ultimately resolves into clean, deterministic pipeline behavior across the machine faces.

Yes, it is entirely possible, and it is actually much easier than writing 3D matrix math or custom block renderers.

Since you are already inside a GUI screen (`GuiGraphics`), you can grab the block's texture atlas sprites and draw them directly onto those configuration buttons instead of flat red/gray rectangle fills.

### How to Implement It

You can replace the solid background fills in your button-drawing method with texture blitting. Because the texture atlas handles stitching, you can fetch each face's sprite (the base glow texture, or a dedicated icon texture) and draw it directly inside the button bounds.

Here is how you can update your button rendering logic in `IoModuleItem.java` to draw the face textures:

```java
private void drawConfigButton(GuiGraphics graphics, net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font, int x, int y, String faceLabel, FaceMode mode, RelativeSide side) {
    // 1. Draw button background container
    graphics.fill(x, y, x + 16, y + 16, 0xFF888888);

    // 2. Bind and blit the actual block face texture from the texture atlas
    String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
    net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite sprite = net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.getInstance()
            .getTextureAtlas(net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
            .apply(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));

    // Draw the texture sprite inside the button (1x1 pixel offset for inner border look)
    graphics.blit(x + 1, y + 1, 0, 14, 14, sprite);

    // 3. Optional: Draw a semi-transparent color tint overlay based on the FaceMode color
    if (mode != null && mode != FaceMode.DISABLED) {
        int color = mode.getColor();
        // Apply tint with alpha blending over the texture
        graphics.fill(x + 1, y + 1, x + 15, y + 15, (color & 0x00FFFFFF) | 0x66000000); 
    }

    // 4. Draw the text label on top
    String charLabel = mode != null ? mode.getLabelChar() : "D";
    graphics.drawCenteredString(font, faceLabel + ":" + charLabel, x + 8, y + 4, 0xFFFFFF);
}
```

### Why this works seamlessly:

- **`InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS`**: Minecraft stitches all block textures into this atlas, so you can pull any side's texture dynamically using its `ResourceLocation`.
- **`graphics.blit` with Sprite**: NeoForge/Minecraft GUI graphics allow blitting a `TextureAtlasSprite` directly at screen coordinates (`x`, `y`, `z`, `width`, `height`, `sprite`), handling UV mapping automatically.
- **Color Tinting**: By drawing a semi-transparent color block over the texture (`0x66000000` alpha mask), the texture pattern stays completely visible underneath while clearly indicating whether the face is set to Input, Output, or Open.

### You

thing is... the block has 2 layers of emissive textures that change dynamically, would those render too

### Gemini

Not automatically with a basic static blit. By default, the code from the previous turn would only draw the base texture with a flat tint.

However, **yes, you can make both dynamic layers render right inside the GUI buttons** by replicating your 3D rendering logic in 2D. Because `GuiGraphics` runs on the client every frame, you can feed the exact same time-based calculations into your GUI button renderer.

### How to Implement Dynamic 2-Layer GUI Rendering

You can update `drawConfigButton` in `IoModuleItem.java` to calculate the rainbow hue and draw both layers sequentially:

```java
private void drawConfigButton(GuiGraphics graphics, net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font, int x, int y, String faceLabel, FaceMode mode, RelativeSide side) {
    // 1. Button background container
    graphics.fill(x, y, x + 16, y + 16, 0xFF222222);

    net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc = net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.getInstance();
    long time = mc.level != null ? mc.level.getGameTime() : System.currentTimeMillis() / 50;

    // 2. Layer 1: Dynamic Rainbow Glow Texture
    String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
    net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite baseSprite = mc.getTextureAtlas(net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
            .apply(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));

    // Calculate rainbow pulse identical to your 3D renderer
    float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
    int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
    float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
    int r = (int) (((rgb >> 16) & 0xFF) * pulse);
    int g = (int) (((rgb >> 8) & 0xFF) * pulse);
    int b = (int) ((rgb & 0xFF) * pulse);

    // Draw base sprite with rainbow tint (using ARGB integer)
    int rainbowColor = 0xFF000000 | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
    graphics.blit(x + 1, y + 1, 0, 14, 14, baseSprite, rainbowColor);

    // 3. Layer 2: IO Module Status Overlay (if active)
    if (mode != null && mode != FaceMode.DISABLED) {
        net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = mc.getTextureAtlas(net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                .apply(net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));

        int ioColor;
        if (mode == FaceMode.OPEN) {
            float cycle = (float) ((Math.sin(time * 0.15f) + 1.0f) * 0.5f);
            int ioR = (int) (0x33 + (0xCC - 0x33) * cycle);
            int ioG = (int) (0x66 + (0x33 - 0x66) * cycle);
            int ioB = (int) (0xCC + (0x33 - 0xCC) * cycle);
            ioColor = 0xFF000000 | (ioR << 16) | (ioG << 8) | ioB;
        } else {
            ioColor = mode.getColor() | 0xFF000000;
        }

        graphics.blit(x + 1, y + 1, 0, 14, 14, ioSprite, ioColor);
    }

    // 4. Text label on top
    String charLabel = mode != null ? mode.getLabelChar() : "D";
    graphics.drawCenteredString(font, faceLabel + ":" + charLabel, x + 8, y + 4, 0xFFFFFF);
}
```

### Why this results in a polished look

- **Synchronized Animation:** The buttons in the menu pulse with the exact same rainbow rhythm and color-cycling rules as the physical block sitting in the world.
- **Direct Visual Feedback:** Players immediately see live updates inside the configuration menu the moment they change a face mode.
