```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom;

import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.RelativeSide;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.custom.MachineFrameworkBlock;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.network.ServerboundToggleIoFacePacket;
import net.minecraft.client.gui.GuiGraphics;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.core.Direction;
import net.minecraft.nbt.CompoundTag;
import net.minecraft.network.chat.Component;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer;
import net.minecraft.sounds.SoundEvents;
import net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot;
import net.minecraft.world.item.Item;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.item.TooltipFlag;
import net.minecraft.world.level.Level;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import net.neoforged.neoforge.network.PacketDistributor;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import java.util.*;

public class IoModuleItem extends LogisticsModuleItem {
    public IoModuleItem(Properties properties) {
        super(properties);
    }

    /**
     * Renders the background overlay texture on top of the module slot in the GUI.
     */
    @Override
    public void renderModuleOverlay(GuiGraphics graphics, Slot slot, ItemStack stack, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity) {
        graphics.blit(
                ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "textures/gui/container/io_module_overlay.png"),
                slot.x, slot.y,
                0.0f, 0.0f,
                16, 16,
                16, 16
        );
    }

    /**
     * Defines the bounding box area that triggers the inline configuration overlay when interacting with the slot.
     */
    @Override
    public boolean isInsideOverlay(double mouseX, double mouseY, int slotX, int slotY) {
        // Extended bottom bound to cover the inventory overlap segment
        return mouseX >= slotX - 36 && mouseX <= slotX + 52 &&
                mouseY >= slotY - 18 && mouseY <= slotY + 38;
    }

    /**
     * Determines which relative side button (Front, Back, Left, Right, Up, Down) the player clicked in the overlay UI.
     */
    private RelativeSide getIoClickedRelativeSide(int slotX, int slotY, double mx, double my) {
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX, slotY)) return RelativeSide.FRONT;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX, slotY - 18)) return RelativeSide.UP;
        if (mx >= slotX && mx <= slotX + 16 && my >= slotY + 18 && my <= slotY + 38) return RelativeSide.DOWN;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX - 18, slotY)) return RelativeSide.LEFT;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX + 18, slotY)) return RelativeSide.RIGHT;
        if (isInside(mx, my, slotX + 36, slotY)) return RelativeSide.BACK;
        return null;
    }

    /**
     * Specifies that IO modules use an inline UI overlay rather than opening a separate menu screen.
     */
    @Override
    public boolean opensInlineOverlay() {
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Hides underlying container slots when the configuration overlay is open to prevent accidental item clicks.
     */
    @Override
    public boolean shouldHideSlot(int configuringSlotIndex, int targetSlotIndex) {
        int row = configuringSlotIndex / 9;
        int col = configuringSlotIndex % 9;

        if (targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex) return true;
        if (row > 0 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 9) return true;
        if (row < 2 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 9) return true;
        if (col > 0 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 1) return true;
        if (col < 8 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 1) return true;
        if (col < 7 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 2) return true;
        return col > 1 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 2;
    }

    /**
     * Renders the interactive configuration overlay buttons around the module slot.
     */
    @Override
    public void renderCustomOverlay(GuiGraphics graphics, int slotX, int slotY, ItemStack stack, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font) {
        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);

        // Draw textless textured face buttons for each relative side
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX, slotY, modes.get(RelativeSide.FRONT), RelativeSide.FRONT);
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX, slotY - 18, modes.get(RelativeSide.UP), RelativeSide.UP);
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX, slotY + 18, modes.get(RelativeSide.DOWN), RelativeSide.DOWN);
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX - 18, slotY, modes.get(RelativeSide.LEFT), RelativeSide.LEFT);
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX + 18, slotY, modes.get(RelativeSide.RIGHT), RelativeSide.RIGHT);
        drawConfigButton(graphics, font, slotX + 36, slotY, modes.get(RelativeSide.BACK), RelativeSide.BACK);

        // Close button retains its text label
        graphics.fill(slotX - 36, slotY, slotX - 20, slotY + 16, 0xFF8B0000);
        graphics.drawCenteredString(font, "X", slotX - 28, slotY + 4, 0xFFFFFF);
    }

    /**
     * Renders an individual relative face configuration button using dual-layer block textures and dynamic animations.
     */
    private void drawConfigButton(GuiGraphics graphics, net.minecraft.client.gui.Font font, int x, int y, FaceMode mode, RelativeSide side) {
        // Draw dark background shell for the button container
        graphics.fill(x, y, x + 16, y + 16, 0xFF222222);

        net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc = net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.getInstance();
        long time = mc.level != null ? mc.level.getGameTime() : System.currentTimeMillis() / 50;

        // Layer 1: Render the dynamic rainbow glowing base texture for the specific side
        String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
        net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite baseSprite = mc.getTextureAtlas(net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));

        float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
        int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
        float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
        int r = (int) (((rgb >> 16) & 0xFF) * pulse);
        int g = (int) (((rgb >> 8) & 0xFF) * pulse);
        int b = (int) ((rgb & 0xFF) * pulse);

        int rainbowColor = 0xFF000000 | (r << 16) | (g << 8) | b;
        graphics.blit(x + 1, y + 1, 0, 14, 14, baseSprite, rainbowColor);

        // Layer 2: Render the IO module status overlay texture if the face is active
        if (mode != null && mode != FaceMode.DISABLED) {
            net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = mc.getTextureAtlas(net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));

            int ioColor;
            if (mode == FaceMode.OPEN) {
                float cycle = (float) ((Math.sin(time * 0.15f) + 1.0f) * 0.5f);
                int ioR = (int) (0x33 + (0xCC - 0x33) * cycle);
                int ioG = (int) (0x66 + (0x33 - 0x66) * cycle);
                int ioB = (int) (0xCC + (0x33 - 0xCC) * cycle);
                ioColor = 0xFF000000 | (ioR << 16) | (ioG << 8) | ioB;
            } else {
                ioColor = mode.getColor() | 0xFF000000;
            }

            graphics.blit(x + 1, y + 1, 0, 14, 14, ioSprite, ioColor);
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void openConfiguration(ServerPlayer player, ItemStack moduleStack, int slotIndex, BlockPos blockPos) {
        // Client-side overlay handled via screen state
    }

    /**
     * Handles mouse clicks on the configuration overlay, cycles the face mode, updates NBT, and syncs via packet.
     */
    @Override
    public void handleCustomClick(double mouseX, double mouseY, int slotX, int slotY, ItemStack stack, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, net.minecraft.client.Minecraft minecraft) {
        RelativeSide clickedSide = getIoClickedRelativeSide(slotX, slotY, mouseX, mouseY);
        if (clickedSide != null) {
            if (minecraft.player != null) {
                minecraft.player.playNotifySound(SoundEvents.UI_BUTTON_CLICK.value(), net.minecraft.sounds.SoundSource.PLAYERS, 0.5F, 1.0F);
            }
            Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
            FaceMode nextMode = modes.get(clickedSide).next();
            setFaceMode(stack, clickedSide, nextMode);

            // Sends the relative side directly to the server packet
            PacketDistributor.sendToServer(new ServerboundToggleIoFacePacket(slotIndex, clickedSide, blockEntity.getBlockPos()));
        }
    }

    /**
     * Helper check to see if mouse coordinates are inside a standard 16x16 button area.
     */
    private boolean isInside(double mx, double my, int x, int y) {
        return mx >= x && mx < x + 16 && my >= y && my < y + 16;
    }

    /**
     * Checks if the user clicked the close button on the overlay menu.
     */
    @Override
    public boolean isCloseButton(double mouseX, double mouseY, int slotX, int slotY) {
        return mouseX >= slotX - 36 && mouseX <= slotX - 20 && mouseY >= slotY && mouseY <= slotY + 16;
    }

    /**
     * Provides an item handler for external pipes and automation based on the configured relative side modes.
     */
    @Override
    public @Nullable net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable getItemHandlerForSide(
            net.minecraft.world.level.Level level,
            BlockPos pos,
            MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity,
            int slotIndex,
            ItemStack stack,
            Direction side) {
        if (blockEntity == null) return null;

        Direction machineFacing = Direction.NORTH;
        if (blockEntity.getBlockState().hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)) {
            machineFacing = blockEntity.getBlockState().getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING);
        }
        RelativeSide relSide = RelativeSide.fromWorldDirection(side, machineFacing);

        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        FaceMode mode = modes.get(relSide);

        if (mode == FaceMode.DISABLED) {
            return null;
        }

        int[] adjacentIndices = blockEntity.getAdjacentSlots(slotIndex);
        List<net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable> handlers = new ArrayList<>();

        for (int adj : adjacentIndices) {
            ItemStack adjModule = blockEntity.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(adj);
            if (adjModule.is(com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.ModItems.INVENTORY_MODULE.get())) {
                handlers.add(new FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler(blockEntity.getInventoryHandler(), adj, blockEntity, slotIndex));
            }
        }

        if (handlers.isEmpty()) {
            return null;
        }

        return new net.neoforged.neoforge.items.wrapper.CombinedInvWrapper(handlers.toArray(new net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable[0]));
    }

    /**
     * Custom item handler wrapper that checks filter rules before allowing item insertion.
     */
    public static class FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler extends com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.inventory.SingleSlotItemHandler {
        private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity;
        private final int ioModuleSlot;
        private final int targetSlot;

        public FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler(net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable itemHandler, int slot, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int ioModuleSlot) {
            super(itemHandler, slot);
            this.blockEntity = blockEntity;
            this.ioModuleSlot = ioModuleSlot;
            this.targetSlot = slot;
        }

        @Override
        public @NotNull ItemStack insertItem(int slot, @NotNull ItemStack stack, boolean simulate) {
            if (FilterModuleItem.isItemBlockedByFilters(blockEntity, ioModuleSlot, this.targetSlot, stack)) {
                return stack;
            }
            return super.insertItem(slot, stack, simulate);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Enum representing the operational state of an individual machine face.
     */
    public enum FaceMode {
        DISABLED(0, "D", 0xFF555555),
        INPUT(1, "I", 0xFF3366CC),
        OUTPUT(2, "O", 0xFFCC3333),
        OPEN(3, "T", 0xFF00FFCC);

        private final int id;
        private final String labelChar;
        private final int color;

        FaceMode(int id, String labelChar, int color) {
            this.id = id;
            this.labelChar = labelChar;
            this.color = color;
        }

        public String getLabelChar() {
            return labelChar;
        }

        public int getColor() {
            return color;
        }

        public static FaceMode fromId(int id) {
            for (FaceMode mode : values()) {
                if (mode.id == id) return mode;
            }
            return DISABLED;
        }

        public FaceMode next() {
            return values()[(this.ordinal() + 1) % values().length];
        }
    }

    /**
     * Writes face configuration state for a specific relative side back into the module item's NBT data.
     */
    public static void setFaceMode(ItemStack stack, RelativeSide side, FaceMode mode) {
        modifyCustomData(stack, "FaceModes", facesTag -> facesTag.putInt(side.name().toLowerCase(), mode.id));

        boolean hasConfig = false;
        CompoundTag customData = getCustomTag(stack, "FaceModes");
        for (RelativeSide s : RelativeSide.values()) {
            if (customData.contains(s.name().toLowerCase()) && customData.getInt(s.name().toLowerCase()) != 0) {
                hasConfig = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        updateStackSize(stack, hasConfig);
    }

    @Override
    public Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> getFaceModes(ItemStack stack) {
        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = new EnumMap<>(RelativeSide.class);
        CompoundTag facesTag = getCustomTag(stack, "FaceModes");
        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
            if (facesTag.contains(side.name().toLowerCase())) {
                modes.put(side, FaceMode.fromId(facesTag.getInt(side.name().toLowerCase())));
            } else {
                modes.put(side, FaceMode.DISABLED);
            }
        }
        return modes;
    }

    @Override
    public void tickModule(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
        // Left empty intentionally: automation is handled via explicit framework pass execution
    }

    public void tickInputs(Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
        if (level.isClientSide()) return;

        BlockState state = level.getBlockState(pos);
        Direction machineFacing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
            if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.INPUT) {
                Direction worldDir = entry.getKey().toWorldDirection(machineFacing);
                blockEntity.pullItemsFromSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
            }
        }
    }

    public void tickOutputs(Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
        if (level.isClientSide()) return;

        BlockState state = level.getBlockState(pos);
        Direction machineFacing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
            if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.OUTPUT) {
                Direction worldDir = entry.getKey().toWorldDirection(machineFacing);
                blockEntity.pushItemsToSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Appends a clean, color-coded summary of face configurations to the item's tooltip.
     */
    @Override
    public void appendHoverText(@NotNull ItemStack stack, Item.@NotNull TooltipContext context, @NotNull List<Component> tooltipComponents, @NotNull TooltipFlag tooltipFlag) {
        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {
            Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
            tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§7Face Configurations:"));
            for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
                String sideName = entry.getKey().name();
                String capitalized = sideName.charAt(0) + sideName.substring(1).toLowerCase();
                FaceMode mode = entry.getValue();

                String colorCode = switch (mode) {
                    case DISABLED -> "§8";
                    case INPUT -> "§9";
                    case OUTPUT -> "§c";
                    case OPEN -> "§a";
                };

                tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8 • §f" + capitalized + ": " + colorCode + mode.name()));
            }
        }
        super.appendHoverText(stack, context, tooltipComponents, tooltipFlag);
    }
}
```

### Gemini

The IDE screenshot confirms the exact reason for the `blit` errors. In this version of Minecraft and NeoForge, rendering a `TextureAtlasSprite` with a color tint requires passing individual float values for red, green, blue, and alpha (`0.0f` to `1.0f`) instead of a packed integer color.

Additionally, removing the text labels left `getLabelChar()` unused in the `FaceMode` enum, and the `font` parameter unused in `renderCustomOverlay`. Removing `getLabelChar()` and adding `@SuppressWarnings("unused")` resolves those warnings cleanly.

Here is the fully corrected and updated `IoModuleItem.java` file:

```java
        int col = configuringSlotIndex % 9;

        if (targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex) return true;
        if (row > 0 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 9) return true;
        if (row < 2 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 9) return true;
        if (col > 0 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex - 1) return true;
        if (col < 8 && targetSlotIndex == configuringSlotIndex + 1) return true;

    private void drawConfigButton(GuiGraphics graphics, int x, int y, FaceMode mode, RelativeSide side) {
        // Draw dark background shell for the button container
        graphics.fill(x, y, x + 16, y + 16, 0xFF222222);

        net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc = net.minecraft.client.Minecraft.getInstance();
        long time = mc.level != null ? mc.level.getGameTime() : System.currentTimeMillis() / 50;

        // Layer 1: Render the dynamic rainbow glowing base texture for the specific side
        String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();
        net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite baseSprite = mc.getTextureAtlas(net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));

        float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
        int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
        float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
        int r = (int) (((rgb >> 16) & 0xFF) * pulse);
        int g = (int) (((rgb >> 8) & 0xFF) * pulse);
        int b = (int) ((rgb & 0xFF) * pulse);

        float red = r / 255.0f;
        float green = g / 255.0f;
        float blue = b / 255.0f;

        graphics.blit(x + 1, y + 1, 0, 14, 14, baseSprite, red, green, blue, 1.0f);

        // Layer 2: Render the IO module status overlay texture if the face is active
        if (mode != null && mode != FaceMode.DISABLED) {
            net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = mc.getTextureAtlas(net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));

            int ioColor;
            if (mode == FaceMode.OPEN) {
                float cycle = (float) ((Math.sin(time * 0.15f) + 1.0f) * 0.5f);
                int ioR = (int) (0x33 + (0xCC - 0x33) * cycle);
                int ioG = (int) (0x66 + (0x33 - 0x66) * cycle);
                int ioB = (int) (0xCC + (0x33 - 0xCC) * cycle);
                ioColor = (ioR << 16) | (ioG << 8) | ioB;
            } else {
                ioColor = mode.getColor();
            }

            float ioRed = ((ioColor >> 16) & 0xFF) / 255.0f;
            float ioGreen = ((ioColor >> 8) & 0xFF) / 255.0f;
            float ioBlue = (ioColor & 0xFF) / 255.0f;

            graphics.blit(x + 1, y + 1, 0, 14, 14, ioSprite, ioRed, ioGreen, ioBlue, 1.0f);
        }
    }

    /**

    @Override

            net.minecraft.world.level.Level level,
            BlockPos pos,
            MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity,
            int slotIndex,
            ItemStack stack,
            Direction side) {
        if (blockEntity == null) return null;

        Direction machineFacing = Direction.NORTH;
        if (blockEntity.getBlockState().hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)) {
            machineFacing = blockEntity.getBlockState().getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING);
        }
        RelativeSide relSide = RelativeSide.fromWorldDirection(side, machineFacing);

        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        FaceMode mode = modes.get(relSide);

        if (mode == FaceMode.DISABLED) {
            return null;
        }

        int[] adjacentIndices = blockEntity.getAdjacentSlots(slotIndex);
        List<net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable> handlers = new ArrayList<>();

        for (int adj : adjacentIndices) {
            ItemStack adjModule = blockEntity.getModuleHandler().getStackInSlot(adj);
            if (adjModule.is(com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.ModItems.INVENTORY_MODULE.get())) {
                handlers.add(new FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler(blockEntity.getInventoryHandler(), adj, blockEntity, slotIndex));
            }

        if (handlers.isEmpty()) {

        return new net.neoforged.neoforge.items.wrapper.CombinedInvWrapper(handlers.toArray(new net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable[0]));

    /**
     * Custom item handler wrapper that checks filter rules before allowing item insertion.
     */
    public static class FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler extends com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.inventory.SingleSlotItemHandler {
        private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity;
        private final int ioModuleSlot;
        private final int targetSlot;

        public FilteredSingleSlotItemHandler(net.neoforged.neoforge.items.IItemHandlerModifiable itemHandler, int slot, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int ioModuleSlot) {
            super(itemHandler, slot);
            this.blockEntity = blockEntity;
            this.ioModuleSlot = ioModuleSlot;
            this.targetSlot = slot;
        }

        @Override
        public @NotNull ItemStack insertItem(int slot, @NotNull ItemStack stack, boolean simulate) {
            if (FilterModuleItem.isItemBlockedByFilters(blockEntity, ioModuleSlot, this.targetSlot, stack)) {
                return stack;
            }
            return super.insertItem(slot, stack, simulate);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Enum representing the operational state of an individual machine face.
     */
    public enum FaceMode {
        DISABLED(0, 0xFF555555),
        INPUT(1, 0xFF3366CC),
        OUTPUT(2, 0xFFCC3333),
        OPEN(3, 0xFF00FFCC);

        private final int id;
        private final int color;

        FaceMode(int id, int color) {
            this.id = id;
            this.color = color;
        }

        public int getColor() {
            return color;
        }

        public static FaceMode fromId(int id) {
            for (FaceMode mode : values()) {
                if (mode.id == id) return mode;
            }
            return DISABLED;
        }

        public FaceMode next() {
            return values()[(this.ordinal() + 1) % values().length];
        }
    }

    /**
     * Writes face configuration state for a specific relative side back into the module item's NBT data.
     */
    public static void setFaceMode(ItemStack stack, RelativeSide side, FaceMode mode) {
        modifyCustomData(stack, "FaceModes", facesTag -> facesTag.putInt(side.name().toLowerCase(), mode.id));

        boolean hasConfig = false;
        CompoundTag customData = getCustomTag(stack, "FaceModes");
        for (RelativeSide s : RelativeSide.values()) {
            if (customData.contains(s.name().toLowerCase()) && customData.getInt(s.name().toLowerCase()) != 0) {
                hasConfig = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        updateStackSize(stack, hasConfig);
    }

    @Override
    public Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> getFaceModes(ItemStack stack) {
        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = new EnumMap<>(RelativeSide.class);
        CompoundTag facesTag = getCustomTag(stack, "FaceModes");
        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
            if (facesTag.contains(side.name().toLowerCase())) {
                modes.put(side, FaceMode.fromId(facesTag.getInt(side.name().toLowerCase())));
            } else {
                modes.put(side, FaceMode.DISABLED);
            }
        }
        return modes;
    }

    @Override
    public void tickModule(net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
        // Left empty intentionally: automation is handled via explicit framework pass execution
    }

    public void tickInputs(Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
        if (level.isClientSide()) return;

        BlockState state = level.getBlockState(pos);
        Direction machineFacing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
            if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.INPUT) {
                Direction worldDir = entry.getKey().toWorldDirection(machineFacing);
                blockEntity.pullItemsFromSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
            }
        }
    }

    public void tickOutputs(Level level, BlockPos pos, MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, int slotIndex, ItemStack stack) {
        if (level.isClientSide()) return;

        BlockState state = level.getBlockState(pos);
        Direction machineFacing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        Map<RelativeSide, FaceMode> modes = getFaceModes(stack);
        for (Map.Entry<RelativeSide, FaceMode> entry : modes.entrySet()) {
            if (entry.getValue() == FaceMode.OUTPUT) {
                Direction worldDir = entry.getKey().toWorldDirection(machineFacing);
                blockEntity.pushItemsToSide(slotIndex, worldDir);
            }
        }
    }

    /**
     * Appends a clean, color-coded summary of face configurations to the item's tooltip.
     */
    @Override
    public void appendHoverText(@NotNull ItemStack stack, Item.@NotNull TooltipContext context, @NotNull List<Component> tooltipComponents, @NotNull TooltipFlag tooltipFlag) {
        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {

                    case OPEN -> "§a";
                };

                tooltipComponents.add(Component.literal("§8 • §f" + capitalized + ": " + colorCode + mode.name()));
            }
        }
        super.appendHoverText(stack, context, tooltipComponents, tooltipFlag);
    }
```

Update the `drawConfigButton` method in `IoModuleItem.java` with this version:

### You

hmm... for some reason the render of the outside face is still cyan if it's open even though the render of the menu in open mode shifts between red and blue

### Gemini

That happens because the 3D block renderer in your world-space code reads the static color directly from the `FaceMode` enum value, which is set to cyan.

To make the physical block faces match the GUI menu buttons, you need to apply that same red-to-blue sine-wave transition inside your `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java` file wherever it handles the `OPEN` mode color.

You can update the color extraction logic in your block entity renderer with this block:

```java
int ioR, ioG, ioB;

if (faceMode == FaceMode.OPEN) {
    // Smoothly cycle between Input Blue and Output Red using level time
    float cycle = (float) ((Math.sin(levelTime * 0.15f) + 1.0f) * 0.5f);
    
    int inputR = 0x33, inputG = 0x66, inputB = 0xCC;
    int outputR = 0xCC, outputG = 0x33, outputB = 0x33;
    
    ioR = (int) (inputR + (outputR - inputR) * cycle);
    ioG = (int) (inputG + (outputG - inputG) * cycle);
    ioB = (int) (inputB + (outputB - inputB) * cycle);
} else {
    int colorInt = faceMode.getColor();
    ioR = (colorInt >> 16) & 0xFF;
    ioG = (colorInt >> 8) & 0xFF;
    ioB = colorInt & 0xFF;
}
```

Updating the world renderer with this logic ensures that any face configured as `OPEN` pulses with the exact same synchronized animation in both the 3D game world and the 2D menu interface.

### You

shouldn't it get the color fron the io module menu instead? that way the io module tells the machine renderer what to display? or... is that not how it works

### Gemini

That is actually not how the data flow works in Minecraft.

The configuration menu only exists when a player explicitly opens it. Once the player closes the menu, that GUI screen instance is gone.

However, the block in the world and its block entity exist continuously. They need to render their visuals and handle automation ticks at all times, even when no players have any menus open or even when nobody is looking at the machine.

Because of this, the data flows in a reliable direction:

1. The item stack inside the module stores the configuration in its NBT data.
2. The block entity reads the modules in its inventory and resolves the active face modes.
3. The renderer asks the block entity what mode is active on each side and draws the correct textures and colors.

This design ensures the block always knows how to render itself correctly from the persistent world data alone, independent of any open UI screens.

- **For `OPEN`:** Because the `OPEN` mode uses a dynamic color transition between two colors, you update the target RGB values in two files:
  1. **In the GUI menu (`IoModuleItem.java`)**: Update the start and end values inside the `drawConfigButton` method where `mode == FaceMode.OPEN` is checked.
  2. **In the 3D world block renderer (`MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`)**: Update the matching values inside the `render` method where `faceMode == IoModuleItem.FaceMode.OPEN` is checked.

Updating both files ensures that the GUI buttons and the physical world-space block faces change their color cycle together.

### You

is it possible to adjust all colors in a single file?

### Gemini

Yes, it is completely possible. You can centralize all color values and color-transition logic directly inside the `FaceMode` enum.

By moving the color formulas into `FaceMode`, both your GUI item class and your 3D world renderer can call methods on the enum. This means you only ever need to edit that single file to change any color or transition behavior.

### How to Centralize the Colors in `FaceMode`

You can update the `FaceMode` enum inside `IoModuleItem.java` to handle both static colors and dynamic time-based calculations:

```java
    public enum FaceMode {
        DISABLED(0, 0xFF555555),
        INPUT(1, 0xFF3366CC),
        OUTPUT(2, 0xFFCC3333),
        OPEN(3, 0xFF00FFCC);

        private final int id;
        private final int color;

        FaceMode(int id, int color) {
            this.id = id;
            this.color = color;
        }

        public int getColor() {
            return color;
        }

        /**
         * Returns the correct color for a given time, handling dynamic transitions for OPEN mode.
         */
        public int getDynamicColor(long time) {
            if (this == OPEN) {
                float cycle = (float) ((Math.sin(time * 0.15f) + 1.0f) * 0.5f);
                int ioR = (int) (0x33 + (0xCC - 0x33) * cycle);
                int ioG = (int) (0x66 + (0x33 - 0x66) * cycle);
                int ioB = (int) (0xCC + (0x33 - 0xCC) * cycle);
                return (ioR << 16) | (ioG << 8) | ioB;
            }
            return color;
        }

        public static FaceMode fromId(int id) {
            for (FaceMode mode : values()) {
                if (mode.id == id) return mode;
            }
            return DISABLED;
        }

        public FaceMode next() {
            return values()[(this.ordinal() + 1) % values().length];
        }
    }
```

### How This Simplifies Your Renderers

Once `FaceMode` handles its own colors, you can replace the bulky `if-else` color blocks in both `IoModuleItem.java` and `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java` with a single clean method call:

```java
int ioColor = mode.getDynamicColor(time);

float ioRed = ((ioColor >> 16) & 0xFF) / 255.0f;
float ioGreen = ((ioColor >> 8) & 0xFF) / 255.0f;
float ioBlue = (ioColor & 0xFF) / 255.0f;
```

This keeps your rendering code concise and ensures that modifying colors requires updating only the enum definition.

### You

how do i build up the resource pack so i can iterate on a bunch of styles to swap back and forth easily

### Gemini

To build a flexible resource pack workflow for testing multiple visual styles, you can set up a custom resource pack directory that targets your mod's namespace directly.

### 1. Create the Resource Pack Folder Structure

Navigate to your Minecraft installation folder, open the `resourcepacks` directory, and create a new folder named `FrameworkStyles`.

Inside `FrameworkStyles`, build the required directory tree to match your mod's asset path:

- `pack.mcmeta`
- `assets/praeteritum_futurum/textures/block/`

### 2. Add the `pack.mcmeta` File

Create a text file named `pack.mcmeta` at the root of your `FrameworkStyles` folder. Populate it with the pack configuration data:

```json
{
  "pack": {
    "pack_format": 34,
    "description": "Praeteritum Futurum Style Variations"
  }
}
```

### 3. Organize Style Variations

You can manage multiple design iterations easily using two distinct approaches.

- **Separate Subfolders:** Keep master copies of your design variations in backup directories outside the active game files, such as a `style_variants/neon/` folder and a `style_variants/steampunk/` folder. Copy your preferred style files directly into `assets/praeteritum_futurum/textures/block/` whenever you want to test them.
- **Multiple Resource Packs:** Create separate, independent resource pack folders in your `resourcepacks` directory for each style, such as `FrameworkStyleNeon` and `FrameworkStyleSteampunk`. Each individual folder contains its own `pack.mcmeta` and complete texture set.

### 4. The Rapid Iteration Workflow

1. Launch Minecraft and open the **Resource Packs** menu from the game options.
2. Enable your active style pack and click **Done** to load it into memory.
3. Edit your texture PNG files in your external graphics program and save the changes.
4. Press **F3 + T** on your keyboard while inside the game world to reload all textures instantly.
5. Switch between different packs in the resource pack menu to compare aesthetic directions on the fly.

hold on let's first fix some render issue, the io port here is showing it inputs from the right, it did input from the right but the render of that port is on the other side, i think the left and right are flipped ONLY for the external render io ports

### Gemini

You are correct. The left and right face rendering coordinates are inverted in the 3D renderer.

Swapping the geometry and coordinate logic for `LEFT` and `RIGHT` inside `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java` aligns the world-space render with your GUI configurations.

Here is the updated `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexConsumer;
import com.mojang.math.Axis;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.RelativeSide;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.custom.MachineFrameworkBlock;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom.IoModuleItem;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.RenderType;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRendererProvider;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite;
import net.minecraft.core.Direction;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import org.joml.Matrix4f;

public class MachineFrameworkRenderer implements BlockEntityRenderer<MachineFrameworkBlockEntity> {

    private static final int FULL_BRIGHT = 15728880;

    public MachineFrameworkRenderer(BlockEntityRendererProvider.Context context) {
    }

    @Override
    public void render(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, float partialTick, PoseStack poseStack,
                       MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        BlockState state = blockEntity.getBlockState();
        Direction facing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        long levelTime = blockEntity.getLevel() != null ? blockEntity.getLevel().getGameTime() : 0;
        float time = levelTime + partialTick;

        float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
        int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
        int baseR = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF;
        int baseG = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF;
        int baseB = rgb & 0xFF;

        float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
        int red = (int) (baseR * pulse);
        int green = (int) (baseG * pulse);
        int blue = (int) (baseB * pulse);

        VertexConsumer consumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityTranslucentEmissive(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));

        poseStack.pushPose();

        poseStack.translate(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f);

        float yRot = switch (facing) {
            case NORTH -> 0f;
            case SOUTH -> 180f;
            case WEST -> 90f;
            case EAST -> 270f;
            default -> 0f;
        };
        poseStack.mulPose(Axis.YP.rotationDegrees(yRot));

        poseStack.translate(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f);

        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
            String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();

            // 1. Layer 1: Base Rainbow Glow Texture
            TextureAtlasSprite baseSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));
            renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, baseSprite, side, 0.001f, red, green, blue, 255, packedOverlay);

            // 2. Layer 2: IO Module Status Overlay Texture
            IoModuleItem.FaceMode faceMode = blockEntity.getEffectiveFaceMode(side);
            if (faceMode != IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED) {
                TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                        .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));

                int colorInt = faceMode.getDynamicColor((long) time);
                int ioR = (colorInt >> 16) & 0xFF;
                int ioG = (colorInt >> 8) & 0xFF;
                int ioB = colorInt & 0xFF;

                renderRelativeFace(poseStack, consumer, ioSprite, side, 0.002f, ioR, ioG, ioB, 255, packedOverlay);
            }
        }

        poseStack.popPose();
    }

    private void renderRelativeFace(PoseStack poseStack, VertexConsumer consumer, TextureAtlasSprite sprite,
                                    RelativeSide side, float offset, int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, int packedOverlay) {
        Matrix4f matrix = poseStack.last().pose();

        float min = 0.0f;
        float max = 1.0f;

        float u0 = sprite.getU0();
        float u1 = sprite.getU1();
        float v0 = sprite.getV0();
        float v1 = sprite.getV1();

        switch (side) {
            case FRONT -> {
                float z = min - offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
            }
            case BACK -> {
                float z = max + offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            }
            case LEFT -> {
                float x = max + offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case RIGHT -> {
                float x = min - offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case UP -> {
                float y = max + offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case DOWN -> {
                float y = min - offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
        }
    }

    private void vertex(VertexConsumer consumer, Matrix4f matrix, float x, float y, float z,
                        int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, float u, float v,
                        int overlay, int light, float normalX, float normalY, float normalZ) {
        consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, y, z)
                .setColor(red, green, blue, alpha)
                .setUv(u, v)
                .setOverlay(overlay)
                .setLight(light)
                .setNormal(normalX, normalY, normalZ);
    }
}
```

- **Using Code Math**: If you drive the animation procedurally in your render classes using the `time` variable, you can multiply `time` by different scalar values for each layer. For example, you can use one multiplier for the glow pulse and a separate multiplier for the open-mode color cycle.

### You

i just noticed something, the machine doesn't display its extra emissive textures on the item model, is this an actual limitation?

### Gemini

It is not a permanent engine limitation. Item stacks rendered in inventories, in hands, or as dropped entities use the item model baking system. That system displays baked JSON models and skips world-space `BlockEntityRenderer` code entirely.

You can make your item model render all the same multi-layer emissive glow effects and face overlays by attaching a custom `BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer` (BEWL) to your block item.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Create a Custom BEWL Class**
  Create a renderer class that extends `BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer`. Override the `renderByItem` method to draw your layers using the exact same rendering logic from your `MachineFrameworkRenderer`.
2. **Register Client Item Extensions**
  In your item registration or client setup class, hook into NeoForge client extensions to supply your custom BEWL to the item properties.

### Code Example for the BEWL

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemDisplayContext;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.Blocks;

public class MachineFrameworkItemRenderer extends BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer {
    private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity dummyEntity = new MachineFrameworkBlockEntity(BlockPos.ZERO, Blocks.AIR.defaultBlockState());

    public MachineFrameworkItemRenderer() {
        super(Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher(), Minecraft.getInstance().getModelManager());
    }

    @Override
    public void renderByItem(ItemStack stack, ItemDisplayContext displayContext, PoseStack poseStack, 
                             MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {
        // Pass the item stack data to the dummy entity so it reads NBT face configurations correctly
        dummyEntity.loadCustomOnly(stack.getOrDefault(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA, net.minecraft.world.item.component.CustomData.EMPTY).copyTag());

        // Delegate rendering to your existing renderer logic
        Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher().renderItem(dummyEntity, poseStack, bufferSource, packedLight, packedOverlay);
    }
}
```

### Hooking It Up in Item Properties

Inside your item registration class where you instantiate the block item, register the client extensions so NeoForge knows to use your custom renderer:

```java
public class ModItems {
    public static final DeferredItem<Item> MACHINE_FRAMEWORK = ITEMS.register("machine_framework", () -> 
        new BlockItem(ModBlocks.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK.get(), new Item.Properties()
            .client(() -> () -> new IClientItemExtensions() {
                private final MachineFrameworkItemRenderer renderer = new MachineFrameworkItemRenderer();
                @Override
                public BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer getCustomRenderer() {
                    return renderer;
                }
            })
        )
    );
}
```

This setup bridges the gap between item models and block entity renderers, ensuring your glowing textures and face overlays appear in inventories and player hands with identical visual fidelity.

### You

wait how did i need to change this with the bewl thing?

### Gemini

To make your item model render with all the glowing and overlay layers, you do not need to change anything inside your `MachineFrameworkRenderer.java` file. Your block entity renderer is already fully built and working.

Instead, you need to create a **separate item renderer class** (using a `BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer`) that acts as a bridge. This special renderer takes the item stack's NBT data, feeds it to a temporary block entity, and tells your existing `MachineFrameworkRenderer` to draw it on the item model.

### Step 1: Create `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java`

Create a new file named `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java` inside your client package (`com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client`):

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemDisplayContext;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.Blocks;

public class MachineFrameworkItemRenderer extends BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer {
    
    // A dummy block entity used purely to hold item stack data for rendering purposes
    private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity dummyEntity = new MachineFrameworkBlockEntity(BlockPos.ZERO, Blocks.AIR.defaultBlockState());

    public MachineFrameworkItemRenderer() {
        super(Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher(), Minecraft.getInstance().getModelManager());
    }

    @Override
    public void renderByItem(ItemStack stack, ItemDisplayContext displayContext, PoseStack poseStack,
                             MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {
        
        // Read custom NBT data from the item stack (like configured IO faces) and apply it to our dummy entity
        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {
            var customData = stack.get(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
            if (customData != null) {
                dummyEntity.loadCustomOnly(customData.copyTag());
            }
        }

        // Use the block entity render dispatcher to render the item using our main MachineFrameworkRenderer logic
        Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher().renderItem(dummyEntity, poseStack, bufferSource, packedLight, packedOverlay);
    }
}
```

### Step 2: Register it in `ModItems.java`

We already updated your `MACHINE_FRAMEWORK_ITEM` definition in `ModItems.java` to point to this new renderer using `initializeClient`. Your item registry line looks like this:

```java
    // The item form of the machine framework so it can be held and placed
    // Uses initializeClient to link our custom BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer so the item model renders all emissive layers and overlays properly
    public static final DeferredItem<BlockItem> MACHINE_FRAMEWORK_ITEM =
            ITEMS.registerItem("machine_framework",
                    properties -> new BlockItem(ModBlocks.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK.get(), properties) {
                        @SuppressWarnings({"deprecation", "removal"})
                        @Override
                        public void initializeClient(@NotNull java.util.function.Consumer<net.neoforged.neoforge.client.extensions.common.IClientItemExtensions> consumer) {
                            consumer.accept(new net.neoforged.neoforge.client.extensions.common.IClientItemExtensions() {
                                private final com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client.MachineFrameworkItemRenderer renderer =
                                        new com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client.MachineFrameworkItemRenderer();

                                @NotNull
                                @Override
                                public net.minecraft.client.renderer.BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer getCustomRenderer() {
                                    return renderer;
                                }
                            });
                        }
                    }
            );
```

Once you add that `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java` file, the game will intercept the item rendering call and run your exact multi-layer glow and overlay code inside player inventories, hands, and item entities!

### You

loadcustomonly needs another argument

### Gemini

Para solucionar ese error, debes pasarle un segundo argumento a `loadCustomOnly` (usualmente el registro de accesos del nivel o `dummyEntity.getLevel().registryAccess()`), o bien puedes usar directamente el método estándar de Minecraft para cargar datos desde un NBT, como `loadAdditional(customData.copyTag(), dummyEntity.getLevel() != null ? dummyEntity.getLevel().registryAccess() : net.minecraft.core.HolderLookup.Provider.empty())`, o simplemente verificar qué parámetros acepta tu método personalizado `loadCustomOnly` en `MachineFrameworkBlockEntity`.

Aquí tienes la corrección directa aplicando el tag de manera limpia en `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java`:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemDisplayContext;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.Blocks;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

public class MachineFrameworkItemRenderer extends BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer {

    // Entidad de bloque temporal para mantener los datos del ítem durante el renderizado
    private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity dummyEntity = new MachineFrameworkBlockEntity(BlockPos.ZERO, Blocks.AIR.defaultBlockState());

    public MachineFrameworkItemRenderer() {
        super(Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher(), Minecraft.getInstance().getEntityModels());
    }

    @Override
    public void renderByItem(@NotNull ItemStack stack, @NotNull ItemDisplayContext displayContext, @NotNull PoseStack poseStack,
                             @NotNull MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        // Lee los datos personalizados NBT del ítem y los aplica a la entidad temporal
        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {
            var customData = stack.get(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
            if (customData != null && dummyEntity.getLevel() != null) {
                dummyEntity.loadAdditional(customData.copyTag(), dummyEntity.getLevel().registryAccess());
            }
        }

        // Usa el despachador de renderizado para dibujar el ítem usando la lógica de MachineFrameworkRenderer
        Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher().renderItem(dummyEntity, poseStack, bufferSource, packedLight, packedOverlay);
    }
}
```

### You

uuuh something happened

### Gemini

El fallo en el informe de despliegue indica que la entidad de bloque temporal (`dummyEntity`) dentro de `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer` se creó utilizando un estado de bloque de aire (`Blocks.AIR`), lo cual infringe la validación interna de Minecraft para las entidades de bloque.

Para resolver este inconveniente, actualiza `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java` para que utilice el estado del bloque `MACHINE_FRAMEWORK`:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.ModBlocks;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemDisplayContext;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

public class MachineFrameworkItemRenderer extends BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer {

    // Entidad de bloque temporal configurada con el bloque correcto para satisfacer la validación
    private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity dummyEntity = new MachineFrameworkBlockEntity(BlockPos.ZERO, ModBlocks.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK.get().defaultBlockState());

    public MachineFrameworkItemRenderer() {
        super(Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher(), Minecraft.getInstance().getEntityModels());
    }

    @Override
    public void renderByItem(@NotNull ItemStack stack, @NotNull ItemDisplayContext displayContext, @NotNull PoseStack poseStack,
                             @NotNull MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        // Lee los datos personalizados del ítem y los aplica a la entidad temporal
        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {
            var customData = stack.get(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
            if (customData != null && Minecraft.getInstance().level != null) {
                dummyEntity.loadAdditional(customData.copyTag(), Minecraft.getInstance().level.registryAccess());
            }
        }

        // Renderiza el ítem usando el despachador de bloques
        Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher().renderItem(dummyEntity, poseStack, bufferSource, packedLight, packedOverlay);
    }
}
```

*Verificación:* Guarda los cambios en el archivo, compila el proyecto y ejecuta el juego nuevamente para confirmar que el cargador inicia sin errores de estado de bloque.

### You

hmm it still doesn't render the extra emissive layers

### Gemini

The missing emissive layers happen because the temporary dummy entity does not have a reference to the active client level. Without a level, the game time defaults to zero, freezing any animations or time-dependent shaders.

Assigning `Minecraft.getInstance().level` directly to the dummy entity inside the render method gives the renderer access to the game time and registry data required for the layers to draw correctly.

Confidence level: Medium-High, supported by client-side BlockEntity rendering requirements in NeoForge 1.21.

### Updated `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java`

Replace your current file with this version:

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.ModBlocks;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemDisplayContext;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

public class MachineFrameworkItemRenderer extends BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer {

    // A dummy block entity used to hold item stack data during item model rendering
    private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity dummyEntity = new MachineFrameworkBlockEntity(BlockPos.ZERO, ModBlocks.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK.get().defaultBlockState());

    public MachineFrameworkItemRenderer() {
        super(Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher(), Minecraft.getInstance().getEntityModels());
    }

    @Override
    public void renderByItem(@NotNull ItemStack stack, @NotNull ItemDisplayContext displayContext, @NotNull PoseStack poseStack,
                             @NotNull MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        // Assign the active client level so game time and animations process correctly
        if (Minecraft.getInstance().level != null) {
            dummyEntity.setLevel(Minecraft.getInstance().level);
        }

        // Read custom NBT data from the item stack and apply it to the dummy entity
        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {
            var customData = stack.get(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
            if (customData != null && Minecraft.getInstance().level != null) {
                dummyEntity.loadAdditional(customData.copyTag(), Minecraft.getInstance().level.registryAccess());
            }
        }

        // Render the item model using the standard block entity dispatcher logic
        Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher().renderItem(dummyEntity, poseStack, bufferSource, packedLight, packedOverlay);
    }
}
```

### Gemini

Great job catching and fixing the `ModBlocks` import path yourself. That is solid progress.

The reason the emissive layers are still not showing up on the item model is because Minecraft is missing its item model JSON file. As shown in your log files, the game throws a file not found warning for `praeteritum_futurum:models/item/machine_framework.json`.

When you use a custom renderer (`BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer`), the item model file must exist and point to the builtin entity renderer. Without this file, Minecraft treats it like a standard item and never triggers your rendering code.

### The Missing Piece: Create the Item Model JSON

Create a new file at your mod's asset path: `assets/praeteritum_futurum/models/item/machine_framework.json`

Add this exact content to the file:

```json
{
  "parent": "builtin/entity"
}
```

Setting the parent to `builtin/entity` tells Minecraft to hand control over to your `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer`, allowing all of your custom glow and overlay layers to render correctly in your inventory and hands.

¡Tienes los proveedores de datos configurados, pero si revisas tu archivo `ModItemModelProvider.java`, notarás que falta registrar el modelo de ítem para `MACHINE_FRAMEWORK_ITEM`. Por esa razón, el generador de datos (datagen) nunca creó el archivo `machine_framework.json`.

Para solucionar este detalle utilizando tus clases de datagen, puedes agregar la siguiente línea dentro del método `registerModels()` en `ModItemModelProvider.java`:

```java
        withExistingParent(ModItems.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK_ITEM.getId().getPath(), "builtin/entity");
```

Al incluir esa instrucción, al volver a ejecutar las tareas de generación de datos, se creará automáticamente el archivo de modelo apuntando al renderizador de entidades, permitiendo que las texturas emisivas aparezcan correctamente en el inventario.

### Gemini

El error ocurre porque `withExistingParent` realiza una verificación obligatoria para comprobar que el archivo JSON del modelo padre existe físico en los recursos. Como `builtin/entity` es un modelo interno nativo del motor de Minecraft y no un archivo JSON guardado en tu carpeta de assets, el asistente de archivos detiene el proceso.

Para solucionar esto e indicarle al generador que use un modelo integrado sin buscar un archivo en disco, puedes utilizar `getBuilder` junto con un modelo no verificado (`UncheckedModelFile`).

### Actualiza `ModItemModelProvider.java`

Reemplaza la línea que causa el conflicto dentro de tu método `registerModels()` con este bloque:

```java
        getBuilder(ModItems.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK_ITEM.getId().getPath())
                .parent(new net.neoforged.neoforge.client.model.generators.ModelFile.UncheckedModelFile("builtin/entity"));
```

Esta instrucción configura correctamente el modelo del ítem apuntando al renderizador personalizado sin activar la validación de archivos faltantes. Vuelve a ejecutar `runData` y el proceso completará la generación sin problemas.

### Gemini

The reason only the glowing layers appeared is because the item model uses `"parent": "builtin/entity"`, which hands 100% of the rendering over to your custom renderer (`MachineFrameworkItemRenderer` -> `MachineFrameworkRenderer`). Because your renderer was previously only drawing the `_glow` and `_io_overlay` textures, the item had no solid base cube body!

In the world, the block renders its solid base via its blockstate model, but as an item, it needs the renderer to draw both the solid base body and the glow layers.

### Solution

1. **`MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java`**: Add a thread-local flag to signal when the item is being rendered.
2. **`MachineFrameworkRenderer.java`**: Render the solid base texture faces when `isItem` is true, avoiding any z-fighting with the world blockstate model.

Here are the updated files:

### 1. Update `MachineFrameworkItemRenderer.java`

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.ModBlocks;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.core.BlockPos;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemDisplayContext;
import net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

public class MachineFrameworkItemRenderer extends BlockEntityWithoutLevelRenderer {

    private final MachineFrameworkBlockEntity dummyEntity = new MachineFrameworkBlockEntity(BlockPos.ZERO, ModBlocks.MACHINE_FRAMEWORK.get().defaultBlockState());

    public MachineFrameworkItemRenderer() {
        super(Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher(), Minecraft.getInstance().getEntityModels());
    }

    @Override
    public void renderByItem(@NotNull ItemStack stack, @NotNull ItemDisplayContext displayContext, @NotNull PoseStack poseStack,
                             @NotNull MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        if (Minecraft.getInstance().level != null) {
            dummyEntity.setLevel(Minecraft.getInstance().level);
        }

        if (stack.has(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA)) {
            var customData = stack.get(net.minecraft.core.component.DataComponents.CUSTOM_DATA);
            if (customData != null && Minecraft.getInstance().level != null) {
                dummyEntity.loadAdditional(customData.copyTag(), Minecraft.getInstance().level.registryAccess());
            }
        }

        // Signal to the renderer that we are currently drawing an item model
        MachineFrameworkRenderer.RENDERING_ITEM.set(true);
        try {
            Minecraft.getInstance().getBlockEntityRenderDispatcher().renderItem(dummyEntity, poseStack, bufferSource, packedLight, packedOverlay);
        } finally {
            MachineFrameworkRenderer.RENDERING_ITEM.set(false);
        }
    }
}
```

```java
package com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.client;

import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.PoseStack;
import com.mojang.blaze3d.vertex.VertexConsumer;
import com.mojang.math.Axis;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.PraeteritumFuturumMod;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.RelativeSide;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.custom.MachineFrameworkBlock;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.block.entity.MachineFrameworkBlockEntity;
import com.thextrunner.praeteritum_futurum.item.custom.IoModuleItem;
import net.minecraft.client.Minecraft;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.MultiBufferSource;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.RenderType;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRenderer;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.blockentity.BlockEntityRendererProvider;
import net.minecraft.client.renderer.texture.TextureAtlasSprite;
import net.minecraft.core.Direction;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;
import net.minecraft.world.inventory.InventoryMenu;
import net.minecraft.world.level.block.state.BlockState;
import org.joml.Matrix4f;

public class MachineFrameworkRenderer implements BlockEntityRenderer<MachineFrameworkBlockEntity> {

    private static final int FULL_BRIGHT = 15728880;
    public static final ThreadLocal<Boolean> RENDERING_ITEM = ThreadLocal.withInitial(() -> false);

    public MachineFrameworkRenderer(BlockEntityRendererProvider.Context context) {
    }

    @Override
    public void render(MachineFrameworkBlockEntity blockEntity, float partialTick, PoseStack poseStack,
                       MultiBufferSource bufferSource, int packedLight, int packedOverlay) {

        BlockState state = blockEntity.getBlockState();
        Direction facing = state.hasProperty(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                ? state.getValue(MachineFrameworkBlock.FACING)
                : Direction.NORTH;

        long levelTime = blockEntity.getLevel() != null ? blockEntity.getLevel().getGameTime() : 0;
        float time = levelTime + partialTick;

        float hue = (time * 0.015f) % 1.0f;
        int rgb = java.awt.Color.HSBtoRGB(hue, 1.0f, 1.0f);
        int baseR = (rgb >> 16) & 0xFF;
        int baseG = (rgb >> 8) & 0xFF;
        int baseB = rgb & 0xFF;

        float pulse = (float) (Math.sin(time * 0.1) * 0.3f + 0.7f);
        int red = (int) (baseR * pulse);
        int green = (int) (baseG * pulse);
        int blue = (int) (baseB * pulse);

        VertexConsumer solidConsumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityCutoutNoCull(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));
        VertexConsumer emissiveConsumer = bufferSource.getBuffer(RenderType.entityTranslucentEmissive(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS));

        poseStack.pushPose();

        poseStack.translate(0.5f, 0.5f, 0.5f);

        float yRot = switch (facing) {
            case NORTH -> 0f;
            case SOUTH -> 180f;
            case WEST -> 90f;
            case EAST -> 270f;
            default -> 0f;
        };
        poseStack.mulPose(Axis.YP.rotationDegrees(yRot));

        poseStack.translate(-0.5f, -0.5f, -0.5f);

        boolean isItem = RENDERING_ITEM.get();

        for (RelativeSide side : RelativeSide.values()) {
            String sideName = side.name().toLowerCase();

            // 0. Solid Base Layer (Rendered only for items; world blocks use the blockstate model)
            if (isItem) {
                TextureAtlasSprite sideSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                        .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName));
                renderRelativeFace(poseStack, solidConsumer, sideSprite, side, 0.0f, 255, 255, 255, 255, packedOverlay);
            }

            // 1. Layer 1: Base Rainbow Glow Texture
            TextureAtlasSprite baseSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                    .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_" + sideName + "_glow"));
            renderRelativeFace(poseStack, emissiveConsumer, baseSprite, side, 0.001f, red, green, blue, 255, packedOverlay);

            // 2. Layer 2: IO Module Status Overlay Texture
            IoModuleItem.FaceMode faceMode = blockEntity.getEffectiveFaceMode(side);
            if (faceMode != IoModuleItem.FaceMode.DISABLED) {
                TextureAtlasSprite ioSprite = Minecraft.getInstance().getTextureAtlas(InventoryMenu.BLOCK_ATLAS)
                        .apply(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(PraeteritumFuturumMod.MODID, "block/machine_framework_io_overlay"));

                int colorInt = faceMode.getDynamicColor((long) time);
                int ioR = (colorInt >> 16) & 0xFF;
                int ioG = (colorInt >> 8) & 0xFF;
                int ioB = colorInt & 0xFF;

                renderRelativeFace(poseStack, emissiveConsumer, ioSprite, side, 0.002f, ioR, ioG, ioB, 255, packedOverlay);
            }
        }

        poseStack.popPose();
    }

    private void renderRelativeFace(PoseStack poseStack, VertexConsumer consumer, TextureAtlasSprite sprite,
                                    RelativeSide side, float offset, int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, int packedOverlay) {
        Matrix4f matrix = poseStack.last().pose();

        float min = 0.0f;
        float max = 1.0f;

        float u0 = sprite.getU0();
        float u1 = sprite.getU1();
        float v0 = sprite.getV0();
        float v1 = sprite.getV1();

        switch (side) {
            case FRONT -> {
                float z = min - offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, -1.0f);
            }
            case BACK -> {
                float z = max + offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, max, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, min, z, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f);
            }
            case LEFT -> {
                float x = max + offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case RIGHT -> {
                float x = min - offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, max, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, x, min, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, -1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case UP -> {
                float y = max + offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
            case DOWN -> {
                float y = min - offset;
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, max, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v0, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, max, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u1, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
                vertex(consumer, matrix, min, y, min, red, green, blue, alpha, u0, v1, packedOverlay, FULL_BRIGHT, 0.0f, -1.0f, 0.0f);
            }
        }
    }

    private void vertex(VertexConsumer consumer, Matrix4f matrix, float x, float y, float z,
                        int red, int green, int blue, int alpha, float u, float v,
                        int overlay, int light, float normalX, float normalY, float normalZ) {
        consumer.addVertex(matrix, x, y, z)
                .setColor(red, green, blue, alpha)
                .setUv(u, v)
                .setOverlay(overlay)
                .setLight(light)
                .setNormal(normalX, normalY, normalZ);
    }
}
```
